[p. 319] The camels *tahushshu al-ard*, meaning they gather the herbage. It was said that this is from the speed of their passing, and in it, along with the abundance of gathering of steps by their closeness, there is the meaning of sharpness. From it: *hashsha al-faras* means it hastened. From approaching corruption: *al-hashsh* (with a fatha) is the defective, short palm tree that is neither irrigated nor cultivated. *Al-hushasha* is the remnant of the soul, as one says: nothing remains of so-and-so except a *hushasha*, meaning a slight remnant by which he lives. The phrase of the Qamus: *al-hushash* and *al-hushasha* are the remnant of the spirit in the sick and the wounded. So this is clear in approaching corruption as previously mentioned, and it is also from the division that may accompany gathering. From it: *tahashhashu*, meaning they dispersed. From it: *qillat al-istihsha*, which is the fewness of people. From the sharpness arising from strength arising from gathering: *hashashtu al-nar*, meaning I kindled it and gathered firewood to it. Everything strengthened by something is said to be *hashsha bihi*. *Al-mihashsh* is an iron with which fire is kindled, meaning stirred up. And *al-shuja'* (the brave), al-Qazzaz said, is "mihashsh harb" when he kindles it by his bravery. *Hashsha fulan al-harb* means he stirred it up. From it: *tahashhashu*, meaning they moved. From sharpness in general: *ahashshtuhu 'an hajatihi*, meaning I hastened him away from it. From gathering and strength: *hashsha sahmahu bi-al-quzaz*, meaning when he feathered it and stuck them on its sides. *Hashashaka an taf'ala kadha*, meaning your utmost, the limit of your gathering of everything by which you are strong. *Hashashā kull shay'*: its two sides. *Al-hushsha* (with a damma) is the great dome, because of the abundance of its gathering and the strength of its compactness. [p. 320]

When he described them, glory be to Him, with these base qualities,

he informed that the foundation and root of these from which they arose is the lack of trust in God, due to the absence of faith, so he said: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the hateful, the remote, whose aim is this world, ﴿have not believed﴾, meaning there was found in them no faith in their hearts, even if their tongues professed it.

Since action is not valid without faith, he attributed to this his saying: ﴿So God has made void﴾, meaning by His majesty, His singularity in His greatness and perfection, ﴿their deeds﴾, meaning He nullified their spirits, so they became bodies with no spirits. Thus there is no benefit to them in any of them, because in this world they were mere forms stripped of the spirits, which are the good intentions. For they had no intention in them except to reach worldly ends. This is an announcement that whoever has this world as his greatest concern is not a believer, and that he will be weak at tremors, inclined toward the base dispositions and natures.

Since whoever does a deed that no one else can, even if greater, nullify its benefit except at a severe price, God, exalted, said: ﴿And that is﴾, meaning this great nullification, along with their boldness in seeking and importunity, [at the time of asking] and their lack of courtesy, ﴿for God﴾, with His attributes of greatness before which voices are humbled and sharp tongues are silenced, ﴿easy﴾, because no benefit is [except from Him] [p. 321] and He is the One, the Subduer. As for others, it is difficult for them to do this, because benefit from others, even if it truly comes from them, is overcome by others through intercessions, the presence of distress, or other things upon them. It is as if they, when fear departed, remained submissive and did not free their tongues nor raise their word. So God, exalted, informed, to confirm His earlier saying about their cowardice, that the obstacle He mentioned had not left them due to the extremity of their cowardice. So He said, confirming that and as an answer to one who might say: "Fear has gone, so why do they assail?":

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 20:**

﴿They think﴾ means they suppose, because of the weakness of their minds in this situation, when fear has gone from them due to the intensity of their cowardice and the fear that had taken firm root in them, ﴿the confederates﴾. You know that they have gone, ﴿they have not gone﴾, but rather they have stayed hidden as a deception. He expressed it with ḥusbān (supposition, a weaker form of conviction) because, as al-Ḥirālī (Abu'l-Ḥasan al-Ḥirālī) mentioned in al-Baqarah, supposition is not overpowering in matters that are part of what man is created upon and what has become firmly habitual for him, whereas ẓann (assumption, opinion) is used for what is known, taken from evidence and knowledge. He said: "So the weakness of a scholar's knowledge is ẓann, and the weakness of an intelligent person's reason is ḥusbān."

When he informed them of their state in going away, he then informed them of their state if what they feared, their return, were to happen. So he said, using the particle of doubt to give good news to the people of insight that this is among the impossibilities: ﴿And if the confederates should come﴾, meaning after they had gone away, ﴿they would wish﴾, meaning a renewed extreme desire would arise in them out of cowardice and intense fear, ﴿that they were living in the desert﴾, meaning engaged in dwelling in the desert, in the state of settling and moving about, ﴿among the Bedouins﴾, who are in a place of deficiency in their estimation and whose company is disliked, even though their wish in that moment is impossible. Then he mentioned the state of the doer of "living in the desert," saying: ﴿They ask﴾ every time ﴿about your news﴾, the great news concerning you, following their habit of hypocrisy so that they may keep a face before you, as if they were concerned about you, showing by this an eagerness about their absence from this war [or to conceal their absence and to show that they were among you in the war, by indicating that some event happened to you at such and such a time or place, and they insist on this without shame]. This is because hypocrisy has become a character trait for them that they cannot be free of. This meaning is supported by the reading of Ya'qub (Ya'qub al-Ḥaḍramī), "yasṭālūna" (يَسّالُونَ) with the doubled sīn, the form that intensifies the act of asking. ﴿And if﴾, meaning while the situation is that, ﴿they were among you﴾, meaning present for your battle, ﴿they would not fight﴾, meaning with you, ﴿except a little﴾, out of hypocrisy, just as they did before the confederates went away: sometimes being present with you, sometimes seeking your permission to return to their homes, at other times hindering others by deed once and by explicit speech another time.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 33, verse 21:

When God, exalted is He, had informed about them of these states, which are the extreme of baseness, He turned toward them with a turning that indicates the utmost of anger, and said, emphasizing and confirming it because of their denial: ﴿Indeed there has been for you﴾ O people, all of you, those hypocrites who are immersed among them, ﴿in the Messenger of God﴾ who came for the sake of rescuing you from everything that harms you, and whose majesty is from His majesty that encompasses every majesty, and whose perfection is from His perfection that rises above every perfection, and he is the most noble of creation. Yet you were content to mix with the boors instead of being with him, ﴿an example﴾, that is, a great model, according to the reading of ʿĀṣim with a dammah on the hamzah, and at the lowest level according to the reading of the rest with a kasrah, meaning you equate yourselves with him, while he is the highest of people in rank. It is obligatory for everyone to ransom his noble fingernail, even with his own eye, let alone equate his self with his self, so that he would be with him in every matter in which he is, not differing from him at all. ﴿Good﴾ according to the reading of the majority, by the absolute patience in adversity, and ﴿more excellent﴾ according to the reading of ʿĀṣim, by patience over wounds in his own self, and affliction in his uncle and his dearest family, and all that he did in bearing hardships, meeting opponents, and giving counsel to God, to himself, and to the believers. He expressed this by the description of the message, because it is the portion of creation from him, so that they may follow his deeds and sayings, and take on his character and states. He drew attention to the fact that what compels one to emulate him, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only sincerity in faith, especially faith in the Resurrection, and that the cause of such contentment is a natural disposition in him. ﴿Who hopes for God﴾, that is, in his nature he renews hope continually for Him who is, in reality, the only Great One, so he hopes for His bliss and fears His distance. ﴿And the Last Day﴾, which must certainly come, and in which creatures will be recompensed for their deeds. Whoever is thus, his hope drives him to every good and restrains him from every evil, for it is the Day of Mutual Loss (al-taghabun), because life there is everlasting and a break there cannot be mended.

When he expressed it with the present tense, which implies the continuity of renewal, and from which follows the continuity of the attribute arising from vigilance, because it is in his nature, it results that it be said: ﴿So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was an example in everything,﴾ confirming what is in his nature of hope. Thus He coordinated with it, or with "kāna" which implies firmness, His saying: ﴿and remembered God﴾, who possesses the attributes of perfection, and He qualified it with His saying ﴿much﴾, confirming the meaning of hope mentioned, by which success is attained, and that what is intended by it is that which is constant in both states of ease and hardship.

(p-325) When He had described what befell this battle of hardships arising from terror among the common people, and had singled out the hypocrites among them with what He concluded with, blaming them for failing to take the example of the one whom God had granted leadership over them and exalted above them in steadfastness and remembrance, and had concluded this with what produces firm rootedness in the religion, He mentioned the condition of the firmly rooted, who possess the attributes of perfection, who take the Caller as their model and follow the Guide. He said, conjoining with ﴿There the believers were tested﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11]: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates﴾, that is, those perfect in faith, ﴿the confederates﴾, those whose sight dazed their hearts, ﴿they said﴾, that is, along with what befell them of the quaking and the magnitude of the circumstances: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us﴾, that is, what we see of this terror. ﴿God﴾, to whom belongs all command, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, who conveys from Him, in the manner of His saying: ﴿Did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without there having come upon you the example of those who passed away before you?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214] ﴿Do people suppose they will be left alone?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2] ﴿Or did you suppose you would be left alone, while God has not yet known those among you who strove﴾ [al-Tawbah: 16], and the like of that. So they named the touch of misfortune and hardship, and the trial by quaking and enemies, [as a promise] because of their knowledge of what they would have with God for it, especially on the Day of Recompense, and what follows it of victory, when the matter grows severe.

Since the meaning of this is affirmation, they removed from it the possibility that it was a matter of mere coincidence, and they stated it in a manner that conveys a supplication for the promised victory, in their saying, conjoined to this: ﴿And God and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ [unrestricted, not in relation to a specific object], ﴿God﴾, who has the attributes of perfection, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose perfection is from His perfection. That is, the truthfulness of both of them became manifest in the world of witnessing in everything they promised of good and ill, of what we have seen. And both are truthful regarding what is hidden from us of what they promised, such as victory and other things. The naming of the two is made explicit for glorification and for seeking blessing by mentioning them.

Since this is a statement that could be merely verbal, like the statement of the hypocrites, (p-326) He confirmed it against the hypocrites' suspicion of that, so He, glorified be He, said, bearing witness for them: ﴿And it did not increase them﴾, that is, what they saw of their terrifying situation, ﴿except in faith﴾, that is, in God and His Messenger with their hearts, ﴿and submission﴾, that is, to both of them with all their limbs, in all decree and destiny. And what is part of the explanation of this has already preceded in His saying, exalted be He, in Surat al-Furqan: ﴿And will assign for you palaces﴾ [al-Furqan: 10].

When all who believed were selling their selves and their wealth to God, since God has bought from the believers their selves and their wealth, and some of those firmly rooted in faith did not give faith its due in fighting with their selves and their wealth, as Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) did, (giving) his wealth by leaving all of it, and (giving) his self by exposing it to dreadful dangers, so much so that the Prophet (ﷺ) would say to him on some occasions, "Stay in your place and let us benefit from yourself," and he (ﷺ) said to him and to Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they were to the religion what hearing and sight are to the body, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) on the night of the cave would remember the pursuers and fall back, and the watchers and go ahead, and what was on the sides and move towards it; and among them were those who fulfilled this expedition and what came before it. So Allah willed to honour them with mention and praise, as a fulfilment of what He favours them with, and as an encouragement to others. So He stated it openly and did not conceal it, lest it be restricted to those previously mentioned, and so be specific to this expedition, and He said: ﴿Among the believers﴾, that is, the perfect ones, ﴿are men﴾, that is, of the highest greatness in Our sight. Then He described them with His words: ﴿who have been true﴾.

When the covenant is (held) by those of lofty resolve and pure character, because of the intensity of their remembrance of it and their guarding of fulfilment of it, and their imagining it so vividly that it is as if a great man were standing before them demanding truthfulness from them, He transitive-extended the verb to it, saying: ﴿to what they covenanted with Allah﴾, the One Who encompasses (all) in knowledge, power, majesty and greatness, ﴿concerning it﴾, that is, concerning the selling of their selves and their wealth to Him by their entry into this religion, which is founded upon that; so they fulfilled it in the most complete fulfilment. In this there is an allusion to Abu Lubabah ibn al-Mundhir (may Allah be pleased with him), who was among the great believers firmly rooted in the quality of faith, when he slipped in his gesture towards the Banu Qurayzah, indicating that what was intended for them was slaughter, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Anfal in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ [al-Anfal: 27]. So he left at once and tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque, confirming his own truthfulness, until Allah accepted his repentance, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) untied him with his noble hand.

When He mentioned the truthful ones, and it might have been understood that truthfulness is only by being killed, He divided them into two categories, pointing to the contrary of that in His words: ﴿Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow﴾, that is, has given his nahb (vow/pledge) in his covenant that he would support the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and die before him, and he finished with that and was discharged from his obligation by being killed as a martyr, so no vow remained upon him, like Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Abdullah ibn Jahsh, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' and Anas ibn al-Nadr, who was absent from the Battle of Badr, and said: "I was absent from the first fight in which the Prophet (ﷺ) fought. If Allah lets me witness a fight, Allah will surely see what I do." Then when those who fled fled at the Battle of Uhud, he said: "O Allah, I disown before You what these have brought," meaning the polytheists, "and what these have done," meaning those Muslims who fled. He fought until he was killed, after more than eighty wounds, from a sword strike, a spear thrust, and an arrow shot. Al-Bukhari narrated from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We see that these verses were revealed concerning Anas ibn al-Nadr: ﴿Among the believers are men﴾." End of quote. And others besides these were killed before this, at the Battle of Uhud and elsewhere. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was among those wounded in this expedition, and he ruled concerning the Banu Qurayzah that they be killed and their women and children taken captive, and he did not observe their alliance with his people, nor did he obey his people in their suggestion to spare them, as Abdullah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite had spared the Banu Qaynuqa'. Nor did compassion for them seize him; (he did so) out of anger for Allah and His Messenger (may Allah be pleased with him). Among those who were not killed in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) was Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, one of the Ten (may Allah be pleased with them all) [p. 329]. He stood firm at Uhud and did what no one else did; he kept close to the Prophet (ﷺ) and did not leave him, defended him and shielded him with his hand until his finger was paralysed. The Prophet (ﷺ) then testified that he was among those who had fulfilled their nahb. So the meaning of nahb here is the covenant which is like a vow leading to death. The root of nahb is striving in action, and from here it was used for a vow, because it is what drives one to that. ﴿And among them﴾, that is, among the truthful ones, ﴿is one who waits﴾ for the fulfilment of his nahb, either by victory, or death as a martyr, or simply by complete following.

When the hypocrites denied that anyone could be truthful in what he shows of faith, He emphasised His statement, alluding to them: ﴿And they did not change (their covenant) in any way﴾, that is, they did not bring about any change by slackening or delay. So this is an explicit praise of the people of truthfulness, and an implicit censure of the people of hypocrisy, in contrast to what preceded. Al-Bukhari narrated [from Zayd ibn Thabit] (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "When we copied the scrolls into the codices, a verse from Surat al-Ahzab was lost. I used to hear the Prophet (ﷺ) recite it often, and I did not find it with anyone except Khuzaymah al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him), whose testimony the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made equal to the testimony of two men: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah concerning it﴾." His words "we copied the scrolls" refer to the scrolls that were with Hafsah (may Allah be pleased with her) after the death of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), "into the codices" refer to the codices that Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered. His words "I did not find it," that is, written down, are evidenced by his memorising it. This indicates that when he copied the codices in the time of Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), they were not satisfied with the scrolls alone, but added to them what was dispersed among the people of what had been written at the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in his presence, just as they did when they gathered the scrolls in the time of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 33, verse 24:

Since it was as though it had been said: "It has been understood from the context of this story that the aim is to turn toward Him, glorified is He, and to cut off all ties with anyone else, because He is capable of everything. He suffices whoever turns to Him in every matter, however utterly incapable one may be of it, sometimes through an apparent means and sometimes through other than a means. So why does He not decide the agreement upon the word of peace, so that rest may be attained from all this hardship?" It was answered: this is so that the attributes of might, greatness, justice and others may be manifested completely, along with judgments that the veil uncovers, and that raise, for their full disclosure, the utmost disclosure, the curtains of means. Then He, exalted is He, said, linking it to His saying: ﴿There came to you hosts﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 9] ﴿that Allah may reward﴾, that is, the One who wishes to manifest all His attributes on the Day of Resurrection, to the elect and the common alike, in complete manifestation, ﴿the truthful﴾ in their claim that they believed in Him ﴿for their truthfulness﴾, so He exalts their affair (p-٣٣١) in the world and bestows favour upon them in the Hereafter. Truthfulness is thus a cause, even though it is a bounty from Him, since He is the One who grants them success in it. ﴿And that He may punish the hypocrites﴾ in both abodes for their lying in their claim of faith, which requires [the sale of] self and wealth. ﴿If He wills﴾, He punishes them for hypocrisy, ﴿or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾, that is, by what they see of His truthfulness, glorified is He, in exalting His allies and humbling His enemies by His complete power, while they were certain of the opposite.

Since the repentance of the hypocrites was considered unlikely, given what they see of their firmness in deception and the corruption of their inner hearts, He said, giving the reason for all of this by way of emphasis: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, with what He possesses of majesty and beauty, ﴿was﴾ from eternity and to eternity ﴿Forgiving, Merciful﴾, who conceals sins and bestows honour upon the one who committed them. As for reward for everyone, His mercy is general; but as for the punishment of the hypocrite, it is specific to the truthful, because the punishment of their enemies is among the greatest of their blessings. And in His judging with justice there is also the generality of mercy, for He does not punish anyone beyond what he deserves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 25:

When Allah (glory be to Him) reminded them of His blessing in what He sent upon their enemies from His armies, and clarified the conditions of the hypocrites and the truthful and the secrets He has in that, and concluded with these two attributes, He said, reminding of their effect in what He had broken of custom by turning away the enemies despite their multitude and strength, into a state that no intelligent person would be pleased with for himself, going back to His saying at the beginning of the surah and the narrative: ﴿So We sent﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9] ﴿And Allah repelled﴾, that is, with what He has of (p-332) attributes of perfection, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who concealed what the suns of their intellects indicated of the proofs of divine oneness and the truth of the messengership. They were of those from among the Arabs and others who banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), coming to them from their lands away from Madinah, and oppressing the believers, while they were ﴿in their rage﴾, which necessitated their banding together [then which necessitated their dispersing without any gain], while they ﴿did not obtain any good﴾, neither from the religion nor from the worldly life. Rather, He forsook them in every respect.

Since the repulse might be thought to have come about through a cause from their enemy, he clarified that the matter is not like that, and said: ﴿And Allah sufficed﴾, that is, the Mighty by His power and might, His servants, and it indicates that He did not do that except for the sake of the people of sincerity. So He said: ﴿the believers in the fighting﴾, by what He cast into their hearts of the resolve to withdraw, with the wind and the armies of angels and others. Among them was Nu'aym [ibn] Mas'ud, as has passed.

Since this was a striking matter, he followed it with what indicates that it is easy for Him: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾, that is, the One who possesses every attribute of perfection, always, from eternity to eternity, ﴿Strong﴾, nothing overpowers Him, ﴿Mighty﴾, who overcomes everything.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 26:

When he had completed the matter of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), he followed it with the condition of those who had incited them, who were the cause of their coming, such as Huyayy ibn Akhtab and those who backed him in that and broke the covenant they had made. He said: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾, i.e., who aided the Confederates. Then he specified them by saying, in disparagement: ﴿from among the People of the Book﴾, namely the Banu Qurayza and those from the Banu al-Nadir who entered their fortress with Huyayy. This took place after the expulsion of the Banu Qaynuqa' and the Banu al-Nadir. ﴿from their strongholds﴾, i.e., their high fortresses. It is the plural of ṣayṣiya (the horn of a cow and the like, by which one defends oneself), and is then likened to fortresses.

Since bringing down (from a place of defence) was a marvel, and could take several forms, and was therefore not explicit in humiliation, the soul yearned to know its state, so he made clear that it was humiliation, saying, conjoining with the particle "wa" so that it suits what precedes and what follows: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, i.e., after the bringing down, just as its casting was before the bringing down. Had he placed the casting before the bringing down, it would not have conveyed these benefits, nor would what follows have been so closely suited to the bringing down.

Since he mentioned what humiliated them, he mentioned what resulted from it, dividing it, saying: ﴿a group﴾. He mentioned it with the word "firqa" (group) and put it in the accusative so as to indicate at the very outset that they were pliant in the hands of the doers: ﴿you kill﴾, namely the men, who were about seven hundred. Since he began with what indicates division, of which "firqa" is a part, and had mentioned the greater of the two results arising from the terror, he followed it with the other result, so that the two beloved results would be surrounded by what indicates division (p-٣٣٤): ﴿and you take captive a group﴾, namely the children and the women. Perhaps he delayed "a group" here to convey choice regarding their affair, and put it first with the men because the killing of them was decided.

When he had mentioned the speaking (the people) in both their categories, he mentioned the silent (property), saying: ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land﴾, meaning the gardens and other things. When he had spoken in general terms, he singled out by his saying ﴿and their homes﴾, because a man defends his homes more than he defends other things. Then he returned to generality by his saying ﴿and their wealth﴾, covering what has been mentioned and other things besides it: gold and silver (al-naqd), livestock, weapons, household goods, and others. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided that spoils. For the horseman he gave three shares (asham): two for the horse and one for its rider, just as a foot soldier received one share if he had no horse. He set aside the khums (one-fifth) from it. The distributions (al-maqasim) were made according to this practice (sunnah), and the sunnah (the established prescribed practice) continued in the expeditions (maghazi).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose from their captives Rayhanah bint 'Amr ibn Khunafah, one of the women of Banu 'Amr ibn Qurayzah. She remained for a little while, then she embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to marry her and to place the veil upon her, but she said: "O Messenger of Allah! Rather, leave me in your possession, for that is lighter upon me and upon you." So he left her, until he died while she was in his possession, may Allah be pleased with her.

Since this was a military expedition, its terror spread through the horizons. It humbled the people of polytheism, the Ummiyyun and others, absolutely. The banners of victory were raised, and their standards fluttered across all the horizons. It sheathed the sword of disbelief and drew the sharp blade of faith (p-335) against heads and necks. Until the Prophet ﷺ, who was the most knowledgeable of people in wars and the most far-reaching in opinion because of his steadfastness when the calamities intensified, said: "Now we will raid them, and they will not raid us." He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and land you have not trodden﴾, meaning you will overcome it by preparing yourselves [for victory] over it and by giving you strength near its conquest. It was first the land of Khaybar, then the land of Makkah, then the land of Persia and Rome and others that Allah conquered after that. He had already decided this in this expedition when He showed the Prophet ﷺ those flashes of light while digging the trench: in the first He showed him Yemen, in another Persia, and in another Rome.

Since this was a dazzling matter, He made it easy by his saying: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾, meaning from eternity and to eternity, with His attributes of perfection, ﴿over all things﴾, this and other than it, ﴿Competent﴾, meaning all-encompassing in power.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 28:

When these events had been established, in which Allah alone gave victory through hidden causes that He brought about and concealed matters that He arranged, things which armies, however select and numerous, and tyrannical, arrogant kings could not achieve, what He had previously stated became clear: that He suffices whoever relies upon Him and turns wholly to Him, and He concluded with the attribute of general and perpetual power. It became evident that He is capable of everything He wills, and that if He willed, He would make the treasures of the earth flow along with His friend (walī). It is not permissible for anyone to look toward other than Him, nor to glance with the face of anything besides Him. It was also known that whoever embraces this religion benefits only himself, and the favor belongs to the Lord of the religion over him; and whoever turns away from it, the burden of his turning away falls only upon himself. The religion suffers no harm from the aversion of this one who turns away, just as it gains no benefit from the coming of that one who comes. Allah had decreed that whoever devotes himself to Him, He protects from the world, honoring him and elevating his rank above its baseness toward the precious things that are with Him, because all of its affairs are heading toward decline, fading and perishing; and no one sets his aspiration upon it except a deficient, misguided person. So Allah began commanding the most beloved of creation to Him, and the most honored in station with Him, the one known (al-Ma'lum), to comply with the command to rely upon Him and to turn away from everything other than Him, and that He chooses from the world nothing beyond sufficiency, contentment and chastity. With a choice that brought people closest to him, as discipline for all people, He said, by way of inference from what preceded: ﴿O Prophet﴾, mentioning the attribute of his elevation and his connection to Him, and the informing of the secrets of hearts and the hidden unseen matters, which requires that his thought be free for what he receives of knowledge, and that he not be distracted from any of that by any harm: ﴿Say to your wives﴾, that is, your women: ﴿If you desire﴾, that is, with a firm state, ﴿the life﴾, that is, choosing it over ﴿the Hereafter﴾, and He described it with what makes those of high aspiration renounce it and reminds the one who has intellect of the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿the worldly life﴾, that is, what it contains of expansiveness, luxury and blessing, ﴿and its adornment﴾, that is, which contradicts what my Lord has commanded me of turning away from it and disdaining its affairs, because it is the most hateful of His creation to Him, since it cuts one off from Him. ﴿Then come﴾: its origin is that the commander is higher than the commanded, so he calls him to raise himself toward him; then it became common until its meaning became: come forward. Here it is a metaphor for informing and intending, by the relation that the one informed draws near to the one who informs him. ﴿I will provide for you﴾, that is, with what I have bestowed upon you in kindness, ﴿and release you﴾, that is, from the bond of my marriage, ﴿a fair release﴾, that is, one in which there is no harm, nor any kind of resentment or oppression.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 29:

﴿And if you desire Allah﴾ — with the natural disposition you have — ﴿and His Messenger﴾ — that is, the One who commands turning away from this world in order to ascend to the ranks of perfection that belong to Him — ﴿and His Messenger﴾ — the one who acts upon what he was commanded to do of withdrawing from it, who conveys to the servants all that he was sent with, concerning the affairs of this world and the religion, leaving out nothing of it — owing to the right he has over you and over all people, in that he conveys to them from Allah — ﴿and the Last Abode﴾ — which is the true life, with what it holds of permanence, exaltedness and ascent.

Since it is not the case that everyone who shows something is of high rank in it, He said, emphasizing (ta'kid) as an alert (tanbih) that what He says is something to be affirmed with certainty and that its emphasis is required, in order to repel the suspicion of those whom the condition of humans overcomes, so that suspicions are cast upon him by the people of hypocrisy and others, or who act as one who supposes that or regards its occurrence in this world or the Hereafter as far-fetched: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ (p-338) — that is, with all the attributes of perfection that belong to Him — ﴿has prepared﴾ in this world and the Hereafter ﴿for the good-doers among you﴾ — that is, those who do that while they are in the station of witnessing, and He knows the good-doer from others — ﴿a great reward﴾ — that is, before which the world and everything in it of adornment and blessing is held in contempt.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 33, Verse 30:

When He, glorified is He, brought this wise and sound expression, with the particle *min* (from) indicating partiality (*tab'īd*) as a warning within an encouragement, all of them did well and verified by their conduct that *min* is for explanation (*bayān*). The Prophet (ﷺ) presented this to them, may Allah be pleased with them, and began with ʿĀ'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), the foremost of the good-doers at that time, may Allah be pleased with her and with her father. He said to her: "I am about to tell you something, so there is no harm in your not hastening until you consult your two parents." When he recited it to her, she said, rejecting her hesitation in the matter: "Concerning this, should I consult my parents? I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode." Then he presented that to all of his wives, and all of them followed the example of ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them, so she became a leader for them, and she attained a reward equal to their rewards. This was narrated by al-Bukhari and others from ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

The cause of this was that the Prophet (ﷺ) became displeased with his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, so he swore off them for a month. When the month ended, he descended to them from the upper chamber in which he had secluded himself, and Allah had sent down the verses to him. Then he gave them the choice, and they chose him, may Allah be pleased with them. The cause of this was that some of them asked for greater provision, while the Prophet (ﷺ) did not love expansiveness in worldly life. al-Shaykhān (al-Bukhari and Muslim), may Allah be pleased with both of them, narrated from ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The family of Muhammad (ﷺ) did not eat their fill of barley bread for two consecutive days until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died." al-Bayhaqi narrated the hadith, and its wording is: she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not eat his fill for three consecutive days. If we had wished, we would have eaten our fill, but he used to prefer others over himself." al-Tabarani in al-Awsat narrated from her, also may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever asks about me, or wishes to see me, let him look at one who is disheveled and pale, who did not place one brick upon another or one reed upon another. A banner was raised for him, and he hastened toward it. Today is the training ground, and tomorrow is the race, and the goal is Paradise or the Fire."

Since Allah, glorified is He, had enforced His wisdom in this world that no statement is accepted except with clear proof, He, glorified is He, said, threatening them about what Allah had protected them from. The purpose of this is to make clear that He had elevated their ranks. For this reason He mentioned the actions attributed to them, considering the wording "whoever" (*man*), and to alert to the error of one who thinks that companionship with the noble prevents punishment for excess, and informs that such companionship is only a cause of greater weakness (*idʿāf*): ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾, that is, those chosen by him because of what is between him and Allah, which shows his nobility. ﴿Whoever commits﴾ is the reading of Yaʿqub as transmitted by al-Baghawi, with the second person "you" (*tā' fawqāniyyah*) meaning "whoever" without its literal form. This is an irregular reading (*shādhdh*), transmitted by al-Ahwazi in his book *al-Shawādh* from Ibn Muslim from him. The majority read it with the third person (*yā' taḥtāniyyah*) according to the wording, and likewise "obeys" (*yaqnut*). ﴿Of you a clear immorality﴾, that is, a statement or action such as disobedience (*nushūz*) and bad character, by choosing the life of this world and its adornment over Allah and His Messenger, or other than that. ﴿Clear﴾, that is, evident and manifest in itself, almost calling out to that, of bad character, disobedience, or other than that. ﴿Her punishment will be doubled﴾, that is, because of that. Since the matter was made to seem grave by the use of the *mufāʿalah* form (*yuḍāʿaf*, from the pattern of mutual action) in Nafiʿ's reading, which implies more than two, as has passed in al-Baqarah, He eased it with His words: ﴿double﴾, that is, in comparison to what is for others, because her measure is not matched by the measure of others, just as the punishment of a free person was made double that of a slave, and just as their reward was made double.

The reproach became severe among the beloved, and blame is in proportion to the height of the station. Blame is in proportion to the favor. Each of the forms *yuḍāʿaf* (passive, from the *mufāʿalah* or *tafʿīl* pattern, according to Abu Jaʿfar and the Basrans) or the active form with *nūn* according to Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿĀmir indicates His greatness, glorified is He. The passive form indicates concern with the intensity of the punishment by making it the main subject of the sentence and the agent of the verb's attribution. All of this is an indication that great matters are small to Him, glorified is He, because nothing harms Him or benefits Him, and nothing among things causes a new occurrence in Him that did not exist before. For this reason He said: ﴿And that is﴾, that is, despite its being great in your eyes, ﴿for Allah, easy﴾. So this looks to the station of majesty, grandeur, and greatness.

Ibn Mustafa... no, here is the translation:

When He had put forward the repelling of corruptions, which belongs to the category of takhalli (emptying oneself of blameworthy things), He followed it with the attainment of benefits, which is of the adornment of tahalli (filling oneself with praiseworthy things), so He said: ﴿And whoever of you submits﴾, i.e., sincerely devotes obedience, and the explanation of the reading of Ya'qub with the feminine second-person prefix has already been given, as related by al-Baghawi and al-Ahwazi in al-Shawadhdh from Ibn Muslim, ﴿to Allah﴾, who is worthy that she not turn toward anyone else, because there is none greater than Him, through constant obedience, so she does not depart from His watchfulness at all, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, so she does not anger him, nor ask him for anything, nor choose a life other than his life. For it is obligatory upon every person to purify his thought and calm his mind and inner self, so that he may be fully enabled to carry out Our commands and to perform what We sent him for, namely showing mercy to the servants by rescuing them from the distresses they are in.

Since that might imply limiting the matter to the act of the heart alone, He said: ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with the yaʾ (third-person prefix), in response to the wording "man" (whoever), urging them toward the stations of men; the reading of the majority with the taʾ (second-person prefix) is according to its original meaning, indicating gentleness toward them in the deeds of the limbs and contentment with what is within their capacity, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If I command you with a matter, then do of it what you are able." As for the deed of the heart, there is no acceptance of it without the full degree, which is why "yaqnut" is masculine, not as an irregular form. ﴿Righteous﴾, i.e., in all that He has commanded or forbidden. ﴿We will give her﴾, i.e., by what We possess of greatness, according to the majority's reading with the nun, and Hamza and al-Kisa'i's reading with the yaʾ, on the basis that the pronoun refers to Allah. ﴿Her reward twice﴾, i.e., relative to the reward of other women among the rest of mankind. ﴿And We have prepared﴾, i.e., We have readied and made present, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿for her﴾, because of her contentment with the Prophet (ﷺ), who desires to be free from the world, which Allah hates, along with what that entails of securing a greater share in the Hereafter, ﴿a noble provision﴾, i.e., in this world and the Hereafter. Nothing is nobler than it, for what is in this world of it she is enabled to spend in a manner in which there is the greatest reward, and she does not fear on its account any kind of reproach, let alone punishment; and what is in the Hereafter of it cannot be described or limited, and there is no hardship or toil in it in any way at all.

Since every truth has a reality and every true statement has an explanation, he said, signalling their excellence: ﴿O wives of the Prophet﴾, meaning, you are among the most knowledgeable of people about what lies between him and God, the reports of subtle matters, hidden secrets, and the nearness he has to Him, ﴿you are not like any of the women﴾. Al-Baghawi said: He did not say "like one of the women" because *aḥad* (any one) is general, applying to the singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine. The meaning, then, is: like groups of women's groups. If the nation of women were examined group by group, no group would be found among them that equals you in excellence, because of the nearness God granted you through your closeness to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and through the descent of revelation, which lies between him and God, in your houses.

Since the meaning is "Rather, you are the highest of women," he mentioned the condition for this, saying (p-344): ﴿if you fear God﴾, meaning, you place between yourselves and the anger of God and the anger of His Messenger a shield. Then he based on this negation his saying: ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾, meaning, when you speak in the presence of a non-*mahram* man (a man to whom marriage is not forbidden), ﴿in speech﴾, meaning, that it be soft, sweet and tender. *Khuḍūʿ* is humbling oneself, submissiveness, softness, and an invitation to evenness. Then he based on the softness his saying: ﴿lest he in whose heart is a disease should aspire﴾, meaning, to treachery, namely corruption and suspicion. The use of "aspire" indicates that his expectation has, in reality, no cause, because softness in women's speech is a natural disposition for them, with no affectation in it. So what is demanded of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) is affectation, to bring about its opposite.

Since he forbade them from continuing with women's natural softness of voice, he commanded them the opposite, saying: ﴿and speak a known word﴾, meaning, one known to be far from any place for aspiration.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 33, verse 33:

When he had earlier addressed the wives in speech and placed it first because of its generality, he followed it with action, saying: ﴿And remain﴾, meaning settle and stay constantly ﴿in your houses﴾. Whoever reads the *qāf* with a kasra, namely the non-Medinans and ʿĀṣim, makes the past tense *qarara* with a fatha on the ʿayn. Whoever reads it with a fatha makes the past tense *qarira* with a kasra on the ʿayn according to his reading. Both are dialectal forms (*lughatān*).

When he commanded them to remain at home, he forbade them the opposite, describing it as repugnant, saying: ﴿And do not display yourselves﴾, meaning do not make yourselves conspicuous outside the houses without a pressing need that compels you to go out. (p-345) This is from the command of the Prophet ﷺ to them after the Farewell Pilgrimage to keep to the lines of their (curtained) enclosures. ﴿Like the display of the former time of ignorance﴾, meaning the one preceding Islam and the period before the command of hijab, by going out of one house and entering another. The word *al-ūlā* (the former) does not require a second one, as al-Baghawi mentioned. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it refers to the period between Nūḥ and Idrīs, peace be upon them both, when the women of the plains displayed themselves, and they were beautiful, while their men were ugly, and the men of the mountains were handsome, while their women were ugly, so corruption increased. On this view, the *ūlā* has a second counterpart.

When he commanded them to keep to their houses in order to be free of impurities, he guided them to adornment with what is desirable, saying: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, meaning the obligatory and the voluntary, as a connection between you and the Creator, because prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing. ﴿And give the zakat﴾, as a kindness to creation. In this there is good news of conquests and the widening of worldly provision for them, since life at the time of its revelation was too constrained even for food, let alone zakat.

When he commanded them specifically about what was mentioned earlier, because these two are the foundation of bodily and financial acts of obedience, and whoever attends to them with full attention is led by them to what lies beyond them, he generalized and comprehended all in his saying: ﴿And obey Allah﴾, meaning remembering what He has of the attributes of perfection, ﴿and His Messenger﴾ (p-346) in all that the two of them command, for he was not sent except to command and forbid, to free creation from the captivity of desire.

Since these verses forbade base qualities, and in place of them the noblest virtues, he explained that this was only to honor the People of the Prophet ﷺ, so that the desire for it would increase. He stressed this to repel the delusion of one who imagines that it is for humiliation or some other deficiency and deprivation, saying: ﴿Allah only desires﴾, meaning, and He is Possessor of majesty and beauty, by what He has commanded you and forbidden you of turning away from adornment and what follows it, and turning toward Him, that you turn away from this world and everything that would be a cause for it, ﴿to remove﴾ [meaning] in order that He may remove ﴿from you the impurity﴾, meaning the matter which always entails filth and disturbance, from all blameworthy traits, ﴿O People of the House﴾ (O People of the House being the vocative), meaning from every one who is among those bound to the Prophet ﷺ, men and women, wives, slave-women, and relatives. The closer a person is among them, and the more particular and attached to the Prophet ﷺ, the more worthy and deserving he is of this desire.

Since he used *rijs* (impurity) metaphorically for disobedience, he used *ṭuhr* (purity) metaphorically for obedience, to encourage those of sound natures and upright minds toward obedience, and to repel them from disobedience, saying: ﴿And purify you﴾, meaning He acts in your purity by protecting you from all filth, both physical and spiritual, the act of one who intensifies it, and he increased its greatness by the verbal noun, saying: ﴿with thorough purification﴾ (p-347).

When he had mentioned that, up to where he concluded with purification, he followed it with a reminder of what Allah, glorified is He, had bestowed upon them, which has purification as its effect, namely their being qualified to witness the repeated descent of the angels bringing revelation, which is the cause of every purity, outward and inward. He said, singling them out from the context for their sake, may Allah be pleased with them, and alerting them that their houses are the descending places of revelation and the mines of secrets: ﴿And remember﴾, that is, in your selves, constantly, and recite it to others by way of admonition and instruction.

Since the concern was with what is recited, he expressed it by attributing the verb to it, to show that it is the foundation of the sentence. He said, using the passive form: ﴿what is recited﴾, that is, what is continually followed and maintained in memory and in adopting its character. He pointed them to the honour that was specific to them from it, and said: ﴿in your houses﴾, that is, through the mediation of the Prophet (ﷺ) who gave you the choice, ﴿of the signs of Allah﴾, which has nothing greater than it.

Since what is meant by that is the Qur'an, he joined to it something more general than it, and said, showing the intensity of concern with it by including it in the group of what is recited, relying on the fact that the governing element is known, since recitation is not said of anything other than the Book: ﴿and the wisdom﴾ (p-348), that is, and he disseminates and spreads knowledge adorned with action and action perfected with knowledge, and do not neglect any of that.

Since the context concerns turning away from this world, and wisdom repels one from it, he indicated at the close of the verse that wisdom, while it secures the success of the Hereafter, also brings the good of this world. He said, emphasizing it as a deterrent for anyone who doubts that elevation is reached by its opposite, and the like of that contained in the report of noble lessons: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿is﴾, that is, has never ceased to be, ﴿Subtle﴾, that is, He brings about aims through the means of their opposites, ﴿Acquainted﴾, that is, His knowledge is too fine to be grasped by thoughts. So He makes turning away from this world bring [it] by the most beautiful ways and the most perfect dispositions, even if the noses of all creatures are rubbed in the dust. He knows who is fit for the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and who is not, what benefits people in this world and religion and what does not benefit them, and the paths leading to everything He has decreed and destined, even if they are other than what people are accustomed to. "Whoever devotes himself to Allah, He will suffice him for every burden and provide for him from where he does not expect." Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Saghir, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, from Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him: "Whoever relies upon Allah, He will suffice him, and whoever devotes himself to this world, Allah will leave him to it." Narrated by the author of al-Firdaws and Abu al-Shaykh Ibn Hayyan in Kitab al-Thawab, from Imran, may Allah be pleased with him, also. Allah, glorified is He, indeed fulfilled His promise in His kindness and realized His goodness in His report, by opening for His Prophet (ﷺ) after that Khaybar, so He poured out from it what He willed of His abundant provision (p-349). Then, when His Prophet (ﷺ) died, He opened the great conquests, to protect them from the splendour of the worldly life, from the lands of Persia, Rome, Egypt, and what remained of Yemen. The conquest spread to all regions: east, west, south, and north. He enabled the companions of His Prophet (ﷺ) to obtain the treasures of all those lands and the stores of those kings, until the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were measuring out wealth by measure. The matter increased until "Umar recorded the registers and assigned stipends to the people, [all of them,] even to the infants, and previously he would not assign anything to a newborn until it was weaned, so they would hasten the weaning. His caller called out: 'Do not hasten the weaning of your children, for we assign to every newborn in Islam.' He differentiated among the people in the giving according to nearness to and distance from the Prophet (ﷺ), and according to precedence in Islam and emigration, and he placed people in their ranks, so as to please all the people. Khalid ibn 'Urfutah came to him and he asked him about what was behind him. He said: "I left them asking Allah to add to your life from their lives." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is only their right, and I am happiest in paying it to them. Had it been from the wealth of al-Khattab, I would not have given you it. But I know that there is surplus in it. If it were that when one of them's stipend came out, he bought sheep from it and put them among your herds, and when his stipend came out a second time he bought a head or two and put them among them, then if one of his children remained, they would have something they had come to rely on. For I do not know what will happen after me. I extend my counsel to all whom Allah has entrusted with their affairs, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever dies deceiving his subjects will not smell the scent of Paradise.'" So his assignment for the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) was twelve thousand for each one, which is about a thousand dinars each year. He gave 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, twenty-five thousand, out of the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for her, but she refused to take except what her fellow wives took. (p-350) And he narrated from Barzah bint Rafi', who said: When the stipends were distributed, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent to Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her, with what was hers. When it was brought in to her, she said: "May Allah forgive 'Umar! Others of my sisters are more capable of dividing this than I am." They said: "All of this is yours, O Mother of the Believers." She said: "Glory be to Allah!" and she covered herself from it with a garment. Then she said: "Pour it out and throw a cloth over it." Then she said to me: "Put your hands in and take from it a handful, and go with it to the sons of so-and-so and the sons of so-and-so, from her kin and her orphans." So she distributed it until there remained a remainder under the cloth. Barzah bint Rafi' said: I said: "May Allah forgive you, O Mother of the Believers! By Allah, we too had a right in this wealth." She said: "Then what is under the cloth is yours." (p-351) We found under it five hundred and eighty dirhams. Then she raised her hand to the sky and said: "O Allah, let no stipend of 'Umar reach me after this year of mine." And she died. Al-Baladhuri mentioned this in his book Futuh al-Buldan.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 35:

When He (glory be to Him) had urged toward noble qualities and pure character, and concluded with a reminder of the signs (āyāt) and wisdom (ḥikmah), He followed it with what belongs to those among the People of the House (ahl al-bayt) who are clothed with the perfect attributes to which that calls. However, He mentioned it in a manner that encompasses others besides them, male and female, in conformity with the generality of the call and the comprehensiveness of the message. He said, in answer to the words of the women: "O Messenger of God! God has mentioned the men and has not mentioned the women with any good; there is no good in us by which we are mentioned. Indeed, we fear that our obedience is not accepted." Beginning with the first, most general and most well-known of the attributes of the people of this religion, and emphasizing, because of the multitude of hypocrites who deny the content of this report and others who openly declare (their disbelief): ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men﴾. And since the difference of gender requires a conjunction, He said, informing of the sharing in the ruling: ﴿and the Muslim women﴾.

And since Islam, despite being the most complete and highest of attributes, may be [merely] outward only, He followed it with what realizes it, which is the inward submission (islām al-bāṭin), through complete affirmation with utmost assent. He said, joining it and what follows of the attributes that can be combined by the conjunction "and," to indicate the establishment of those who combine these attributes in each one of them: ﴿and the believing men and the believing women﴾. And since the believing Muslim [man] may not be sincere in his deeds, He said: ﴿and the obedient men﴾, i.e., sincere in their faith and their submission ﴿and the obedient women﴾. And since qunūt, as it is applied to sincerity which requires constancy, may also be applied to obedience in general, He said: ﴿and the truthful men﴾ in all of that ﴿and the truthful women﴾, i.e., in their sincerity in obedience, and that requires continuity.

And since truthfulness, which is the sincerity of word and deed free from any admixture that attaches to it or any thing that defiles it, may not always be present, He said, indicating that what is not constant is not truthfulness in reality: ﴿and the patient men and the patient women﴾. And since patience may be a natural disposition, He indicated its direction toward God by His saying: ﴿and the humble men and the humble women﴾. And since humility (khushū'), which is submission, lowliness and tranquility, is not valid together with the abundance of wealth, for wealth will incline toward it, He said, informing that at that time it is not in its reality: ﴿and the charitable men﴾, i.e., those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God with utmost effort from their souls, [by what the marking of the tā' indicates] obligatory and voluntary, secretly and openly, [also] by what the manifest form guides to, confirming their humility ﴿and the charitable women﴾.

And since the giving of wealth may not be accompanied by preference (īthār), He followed it with what assists in it, and said: ﴿and the fasting men﴾, i.e., voluntarily fasting, for preferring others with food and other things ﴿and the fasting women﴾. And since fasting breaks the desire of the private parts and may stir it, He said: ﴿and the men who guard their private parts﴾, i.e., from what is not lawful to them, through fasting and what fasting stirs ﴿and the women who guard﴾. And since guarding the private parts and all other deeds hardly exists except with remembrance (dhikr), which is that in which there is watchfulness (murāqabah) leading to the presence (muḥāḍarah) that realizes direct witnessing (mushāhadah) that gives life through annihilation (fanā'), He said: ﴿and the men who remember God much﴾, i.e., together with [recollecting] what He possesses of perfection through the attributes of majesty and beauty ﴿much﴾, with the heart and tongue, in every state ﴿and the women who remember﴾. And among the signs of much remembrance is to be constantly occupied with it upon waking from sleep.

And since the obedient person, even if he exceeds the limit in striving, falls short of reaching what is due to him, God (glory be to Him) indicated this by His saying, repeating the Greatest Name as an indication of that and of the smallness of sins when they are compared to His pardon: ﴿God has prepared﴾, i.e., He whom no one can measure with His true measure, although nothing magnifies Him ﴿for them forgiveness﴾, i.e., for their lapses and the evil deeds they have committed, such that He erases its trace and effect, so there is no reproach and no punishment, and no cause for it is mentioned.

And since He mentioned the favor of pardon, He followed it with the bestowal of generosity and mercy, and said: ﴿and a great reward﴾. The preparation of the reward indicates that what is meant by these attributes is their combination, for the one who displays Islam while being a hypocrite is a disbeliever, and the one who leaves out any of the attributes is characterized by its opposite, and then he is deficient in the rest. And what is meant by the conjunction is the firmness and establishment in each of these attributes, in addition to the firmness conveyed by describing with the attribute rather than the verb. Then the major sins are absent, so the expiation of minor sins becomes possible, and forgiveness and reward come. As for the verse on prohibition, it did not use the conjunction, lest it be thought that they (the wives) are types, each type distinguished by one attribute. The conveying of firmness here regarding the attributes comes from the context of favor and praise by their being better.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 36:

When Allah, glorified is He, had already placed before us His saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6] - the verse - it is known with certainty that a consequence of it, whose implied meaning is: "It is not for a believing man or a believing woman to have any choice of their own in the matter of a wali (guardian/protector) other than the Prophet ﷺ," was intended. He omitted this for the knowledge of it, and he cited as evidence for the meaning of this verse and what precedes it the story of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). He followed it with the result of that, from what he mentioned: the disciplining of the wives for his sake, their refinement on his account, the purification of his household and their honouring, until Allah, glorified is He, concluded with the ten attributes which He began with Islam, in which there is no trace of refusal, and concluded them with the fact that the remembrance of Allah fills the heart and the mouth, and it calls to the like of that because it is the cause of Islam. He joined to the consequence of the verse of guardianship what the abundance of remembrance requires, in His saying: ﴿And it is not⦆.

Since faith may be claimed falsely because it is hidden, He said: ﴿for a believing man﴾, that is, from among ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh, Zayd and others, ﴿nor a believing woman﴾, that is, from among Zaynab and others. Thus He tied the matter to faith, to make known that whoever opposes it is not a believer, even if he displays faith with his tongue. ﴿When Allah has decreed﴾, that is, the Supreme King, for whose decree no intelligent person should hesitate (p-355) ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose decree is not known except through him, ﴿a matter﴾, that is, any matter whatsoever.

Since the intended meaning is every believer, and the expression is suitable for that, and negation regarding the whole group is negation regarding whatever is less than it by way of a fortiori reasoning, He said: "that there should be" – that is, a firm state according to the reading of the majority with the feminine prefix, and in the utmost firmness according to the reading of the Kufans with the masculine prefix – ﴿for them﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿a choice﴾ (al-khiyarah), a verbal noun from takhayyara, like al-tiyarah from tatayyara, against analogy, ﴿in their affair﴾, that is, the affair specific to them, by seeking guidance (istikharah) from Allah or by anything else, so that they might act contrary to that decree. For the purpose of istikharah is the presumption of what Allah has chosen, whereas the Prophet's ﷺ report is definitive in indicating what Allah, exalted is He, has chosen. In this there is a rebuke to Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, for making acceptance conditional upon istikharah when the Prophet ﷺ proposed to her for his own noble self, and for her dislike when he proposed her for Zayd, his freedman. But when she advanced, after the revelation of the verse, she gave the Prophet ﷺ the choice in marrying her to Zayd, may Allah be pleased with both of them, according to her choice; Allah compensated her by making her his wife ﷺ with him in Paradise in the highest ranks. So the choice belongs to the Prophet ﷺ, because he does not speak from desire. Whoever does otherwise has disobeyed the Prophet ﷺ, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Allah, because he speaks only from Him. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah﴾, that is, the One for whom no one has any command alongside Him, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, [the one] whose disobedience is disobedience to Him, because he stands between Him and creation in conveying what he was sent with to them, ﴿has indeed strayed﴾, and the verbal noun emphasised it, so He said: ﴿a clear straying﴾, and He increased it by His saying: ﴿clear﴾, that is, there is no concealment in it. Therefore it is obligatory upon everyone to be with him ﷺ in everything he chooses, even if it involves the greatest hardships for him, by the words of the poet when he said:

"Passion has halted me where you are, so there is for me
neither one who lags behind it nor one who goes before it.

You humiliated me, so I humiliated myself willingly,
for whoever is humbled by you is not one who is honoured."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 33, verse 37:

Since He, glory be to Him, had informed him, as al-Baghawi and others narrated from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from 'Ali ibn Judh'an, from Zayn al-'Abidin 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, would be among his wives and that Zayd would divorce her, he concealed that within himself out of generosity and fear of people's talk, that he wished to marry his son's wife. The making of this known was among the signs of prophethood (*a'lam al-nubuwwa*). The foundation of the matter of the Message is conveying to people what Allah has informed him of, whether they love it or dislike it, and that he should not consider anyone else or turn to anything other than Him, even if that entails fear for his own life. For He is sufficient for whoever seeks His might, and He is the perfecter of whoever seeks His wisdom. Just as Allah took the covenant from all the prophets, and from Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and 'Isa ibn Maryam, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, it is known that the implied sense is: "Remember what We took from you and from the prophets as a covenant to convey everything We have told you, and We did not forbid you to disclose it, and what We took from creation in regard to obedience to you and disobedience to you." Then He joined to it His words: ﴿And when you said﴾. This is because the most perfect one may be reproached for some perfections, due to the loftiness of his rank above them and his adornment with something more perfect than them, by way of "the good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near." He showed his nobility by His words: ﴿to him on whom Allah bestowed favour﴾, i.e., the King who possesses every perfection, ﴿upon him﴾, i.e., with Islam and with His Prophet ﷺ taking charge of him after his creation and upbringing. He showed his station with the Prophet ﷺ by His words: ﴿and you bestowed favour upon him﴾, i.e., by manumission and adoption, when he consulted you about separating from his wife, whom Allah had informed you he would divorce and whom you would then have as your wife: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾, i.e., Zaynab, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all greatness, in all your affairs, especially what concerns her rights, and do not wrong her by saying: "She acts above me," and the like. ﴿And you were concealing﴾, i.e., while you were concealing, that is, you were saying to him in secret ﴿within yourself﴾, i.e., of what Allah had informed you, that she would become one of your wives, concerning the divorce of Zayd. ﴿That which Allah was to bring to light﴾, i.e., by causing Zayd to divorce her, even though you had commanded him to keep her, to marry her, and to consummate the marriage with her. This is evidence that he concealed only what Allah had made him know, namely that she would become his wife after Zayd's divorce, because Allah, exalted is He, did not reveal anything other than that. Had he concealed anything else, Allah, glory be to Him, would have revealed it, for "the word is not changed with Him." Al-Bukhari narrated from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that these verses were revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zayd ibn Harithah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

When He mentioned his concealing that, He mentioned its cause, saying, joining it to "you were concealing": ﴿and you feared the people﴾, i.e., [lest] you should tell them what Allah had informed you, so that they would direct at you the arrows of suspicions, especially the Jews and the hypocrites. ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., while the One than whom nothing is greater ﴿has more right that you fear Him﴾, i.e., Him alone. You should not combine the fear of people with the fear of Him by delaying something He told you about because of something that is hard for you, until a matter is decided for you concerning it. 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "If the Prophet ﷺ had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse."

When it was known from this that He, glory be to Him, had informed him that Zayd would divorce her and that she would become his wife after Zayd divorced her, He made the following a consequence of it, joining it to what precedes: ﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need of her﴾, i.e., his need of her in marriage and consummation, (p. 359) and this is by the completion of her waiting period after him, because by this it is known that he has no need of her, that his resolve has fallen short of her, and that his soul has become content without her; otherwise he would have taken her back. ﴿We gave her to you in marriage﴾, and We did not make you need a guardian from among the creatures to conclude the marriage for you, honouring you and her, by the greatness We possess, through which We broke the customs of creation, until everyone who knew of it submitted to it, all souls rejoiced in it, and no hypocrite or anyone else could engage in discussing it with even a word that would weaken or affect him. Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When the waiting period of Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: 'Go and mention her to me.' So Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, went until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough. He said: 'When I saw her, she became great in my chest, so that I could not look at her, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and retreated on my heels, and I said: "O Zaynab! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentions you." She said: "I will do nothing until I consult my Lord." So she stood up to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered upon her without permission.'" He said: "We saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fed us bread and meat until the day extended, and the people went out, but some men remained talking..." and he mentioned it, which will come. Al-Baghawi said: (p. 360) al-Sha'bi said: "Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: 'I take pride over you in three things, which none of your wives takes pride in: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; Allah married me to you in the heavens; and the envoy was Jibril, peace be upon him.'"

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the marriage with the greatness that belongs to Him, He mentioned its cause, [indicating that the basic principle is that the community shares the rulings with the Prophet ﷺ, and that there is no specificity except by evidence], saying: ﴿so that there should be no difficulty for the believers﴾, i.e., those whose nobility in faith has removed their portions of self-interest, ﴿in regard to the wives of their adopted sons﴾, i.e., those whom they adopted and whom they treated, in the prohibition of their wives, as the wives of their real sons [in actuality] are treated, ﴿when they have accomplished their need of them﴾, i.e., their need of consummation, then divorce and the completion of the waiting period.

When He, glory be to Him, knew that people would say various things about this event, He indicated what Zayn al-'Abidin said by His words: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, i.e., [of] the ruling of marrying her, even if you disliked it and left off disclosing what Allah had informed you of, out of dislike for ill talk and out of shame regarding that. Likewise, every matter He wills, glory be to Him, ﴿must be accomplished﴾, because to Him belongs the whole command; there is none to repel His command, and none to reverse His judgment.

(p. 361) When this facilitation yielded what he (ﷺ) had found difficult, and security regarding what he had feared, he expressed this by his saying, emphasizing it as a rebuttal of whoever thinks otherwise: ﴿There is no fault upon the Prophet﴾, i.e., the one whose rank with God is that he is informed of what none of the other creatures is informed of, ﴿in what Allah has ordained﴾, i.e., decreed, by His attributes of perfection, and made obligatory ﴿for him﴾, because there was no fault at all upon the believers in that, so how about the chief of the believers? Thus no fault was negated from him twice, the specific after the general, as an honour to him and an elevation of his status.

Since participation makes difficult matters easier, how much more so when the participation comes from the great, he said, placing the noun in the place of its verbal noun: ﴿the way of Allah﴾, i.e., the practice of the King, who, when He establishes something, perfects it by His might and wisdom, so no one can change any part of it. ﴿With those who passed away before﴾. It seems he intended that the prophets of the Children of Israel, peace be upon them, be the foremost referents of this, as a rebuke to those who confused their followers. So he introduced the preposition and said: ﴿from before﴾, i.e., from the earlier prophets, regarding the permission of widening in marriage for them. This is a refutation of the Jews who denied that, and a disclosure of their deception.

Since the intended meaning of "the way" (al-nisbah) is the path that He decreed and legislated, he said, informing (p. 362) that this marriage was a matter that had to occur, because of His will for it from eternity, so no objector can raise an objection to it with even a word, and whoever does so will suffer what befalls those who opposed the commands of the King. And for the sake of attention to this information, he [placed it between the qualifier] and the qualified, saying: ﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾, i.e., the judgment of the Supreme King regarding that and other matters, of everything that deserves that He command it, guide to it and urge it. He expressed the practice (sunnah) by the word "command" for emphasis, since it must occur. ﴿A decree determined﴾, and he reinforced it by his saying: ﴿determined﴾, i.e., there is no reversal in it, and it must occur at the time He has decreed for it. This is also corroborated by the saying of Zayn al-'Abidin

Likewise is His saying, describing those who passed before (may Allah be pleased with them): ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾, i.e., to their nations, ﴿the messages of Allah﴾, i.e., of the Supreme King, whether they were concerning marriage or other matters, whether they were burdensome or not. ﴿And they fear Him﴾, i.e., so they report everything He informed them of and did not let anything prevent them from divulging it. He alluded, after the explicit statement in His saying ﴿and you feared the people﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37], to ﴿and they fear none but Allah﴾, whether little or great, ﴿except Allah﴾, because He is Possessor of Majesty and Honour.

Since fear of the just King is only fear of His reckoning, the implication is: "so they fear His reckoning." He followed this with His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿as Reckoner﴾, i.e., as the One who recompenses every person for what he has done, reaching the utmost extent in His reckoning, and being sufficient for whoever He wills to be sufficient for, protecting from every person who intends him harm.

**[p. 363]** When this established all of that, that the adopted son (al-da'i) is not a real son, and when they had said, upon his marriage to Zaynab, as al-Tirmidhi narrated from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, "He has married his son's wife," Allah, glorified is He, informed of it in a manner that is among the signs of prophethood and the greatest proofs of the message. So He said: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. That is, in no way at all, ﴿Muhammad﴾, despite the multitude of his wives and children, ﴿the father of any one of your men﴾, neither metaphorically through adoption nor literally through birth. This was so that it would be established that the wife of a son is forbidden to him. He did not say "of your sons," even though he had no son at that time, which was the fifth year or near it. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned, by His knowledge, that a son named Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would be born to him, and despite the sons he had before him, none of whom reached puberty. Peace and blessings be upon all of them.

Since there is a contradiction between his being ﷺ the literal father of any man and his being the Seal, He said: ﴿But [he is] the Messenger of Allah﴾, which was, in Allah's knowledge, hidden and manifest, the Messenger of the Mighty King, to whom everything other than Him is a servant. So between you and His Messenger there is, in terms of the message in general, a metaphorical fatherhood and sonship. As for his side, it is through compassion, mercy, upbringing and advice, without that sonship forbidding any of your wives to him, for otherwise the station of prophethood would have no distinction. As for your side, it is through the obligation of honor, reverence, obedience, and the sanctity of his wives.
