As for the message being from Allah, than whom there is none greater, it necessitates that he convey to people everything He commanded him with. Allah, exalted is He, has already conveyed to you His saying: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5]. The noble office requires that he be the first to act upon this command, so he does not call any of your men "his son" after this.

Since neither prophethood in general nor the message in general is incompatible with the fatherhood of men, He said: ﴿and the Seal of the Prophets﴾. That is, because his message is universal, and his prophethood together with it is the miraculousness of the Qur'an, there is no need with it for any further prophetic appointment or sending. Thus no one born after him will be a prophet. This necessitates that no son born to him should reach the stage of manhood. Had it been decreed that a prophet would come after him, he would only have been from his offspring, as an honor to him. [For he is the highest of the prophets in rank and greatest in nobility. No prophet has a distinction except that he has its like or something greater than it. Had any of his sons become a man, he would have been a prophet after the manifestation of his prophethood. Allah has decreed that there be no prophet after him, as an honor to him.] Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated, from Anas and from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said about his son Ibrahim: "Had he lived, he would have been a truthful man (siddiq) and a prophet." Al-Bukhari has a similar report from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari also has, from the hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa, may Allah be pleased with him: "If it had been decreed that there would be a prophet after Muhammad ﷺ, his son would have lived, but there is no prophet after him." The summary is that no prophet comes after him with a new law at all, and the appointment of a prophet does not renew after him at all. Thus the matter comes to this: the meaning is, "Muhammad is not such that a prophethood with a message or otherwise would be renewed after him. Rather he, despite being the Messenger of Allah, was [the one who was] the seal of prophethood. However, he was presented in the miraculous manner for the reasons mentioned and others." This verse establishes that he is the Seal in the most eloquent and greatest manner. That is because it occurs in the context of denying that any of his sons from among their men would be a son, either literally or metaphorically, through any means other than [descent through a female or] his being a messenger and seal, to protect the station of prophethood from being renewed after him for anyone. For if that [i.e., a son] were a human, he would only have been a son of his. The death of his sons, upon him be peace and blessings, and their effect upon his noble heart [through them] was chosen only to elevate his station so that no one, whoever he may be, would ascend it. This is because the benefit of the coming of a prophet is to complete something that was not brought by those before him, and by him ﷺ completion has been achieved, so nothing remains beyond it. "I was sent to perfect noble character." As for renewing what has weakened through what some sinners have introduced, the scholars are sufficient for it, because of the presence of what was specific to him ﷺ in this miraculous Qur'an, whoever hears it is as if he heard it from Allah, because there is certainty and conviction that no one other than Him can say anything of it. So whenever heedlessness occurs about that, those among the scholars whom Allah wills establish it, and insight returns [as was narrated in some reports]: "The scholars of my nation are like the prophets of the Children of Israel." As for the coming of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, after the renewal by al-Mahdi, may Allah be pleased with him, of everything in the pillars of noble qualities that had weakened, it is for the sake of the trial of the Dajjal, then the great calamity of Yajuj and Majuj, and similar matters which no one but a prophet can bear alone. How excellent is what is transmitted from Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, in his elegy for Ibrahim, son of the Prophet ﷺ, where he said:

"Your son has passed away, praised in his outcome, not stained with any fault, nor blamed by word or deed.

He saw that if he lived he would equal you in exalted rank, so he preferred to remain alone, without an equal."

Al-Ghazali, may Allah have mercy on him, said at the end of his book al-Iqtisad: The Ummah understood from this expression, that is, the expression of this verse, and from the indications of his circumstances ﷺ, that he made clear that there is no prophet after him ever, and no messenger after him ever, and that there is no interpretation or specification in it. He said: whoever interprets it by restricting "the prophets" to the Ulu al-ʿAzm among the messengers and the like, his speech is among kinds of raving, and it does not prevent the ruling of his takfir (declaring him a disbeliever), because he denies this text, which the Ummah has agreed is not to be interpreted or specified. This is his speech in the book al-Iqtisad; I have quoted it from it directly, without intermediary or imitation. So beware of listening to whoever transmits from him other than this, for that is distortion, from which the Proof of Islam (Hujjat al-Islam) is exempt:

"How many a critic has faulted a sound statement, while its defect came from a sick understanding."

It has become clear by this that the coming of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, [is not] detrimental to this text, for he is from the Ummah of the Prophet ﷺ, who affirm his Shari'a. He had been a prophet before him and nothing new was added to him that did not exist. [So that] is not detrimental to the seal, and it establishes the nobility of our Prophet ﷺ, and were it not for him, it would not have existed. This is because no prophet among the prophets had a distinction except that he ﷺ has its like or higher than it. The prophets used to come confirming the Shari'a of Musa, peace be upon him, renewing it. So the one who confirms the Shari'a of our Prophet ﷺ and follows his religion is one who abrogates the Shari'a of Musa, peace be upon him.

Since the context in this decisive ruling that no son born to him will become a man is the station of comprehensive knowledge, the meaning is: because He, glorified is He, has encompassed in knowledge that, despite the multitude of his wives and the number of his children, no male child will be born to him who becomes a man. ﴿And Allah is﴾ [i.e.,] the One who possesses every attribute of perfection, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿All-Knowing of everything﴾ **[p. 368]** of that and other matters. So He knows who is fit for the seal and who is fit for the beginning.

The Ustadh Waliyy al-Din al-Malawi said in his book Hisn al-Nufus on the questioning in the grave: His ﷺ being specifically named Ahmadiyya and Muhammadiyya, as a knowledge and a descriptive attribute, is a clear proof of his being the Seal, since praise is associated with the conclusion of matters and is legislated at their end, and the last of their supplication is "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." Al-Suhayli explained this in the surah of al-Hawariyyun in his book al-I'lam. End of quotation. I have explained in the surah of al-Nahl that the root of the word hamd (praise) revolves around reaching the ultimate goal and mounting the final limit.

Since what He affirmed for Himself, glory be to Him, of the comprehensiveness of knowledge necessarily entails comprehensiveness regarding the attributes of perfection, and since He had promised that whoever relies upon Him He would suffice for every concern, and had indicated this through the story of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and other accounts, and had commanded obedience to His Prophet ﷺ and had advanced the complete charge concerning his exaltation, to the point that He concluded the matter in his honor, and since the servant's obedience to the Messenger of God ﷺ must be in every respect, to the extent that he is stripped of his own choice in his presence, so that by this he becomes a submitter who is moved by nothing but obedience to God, and since obedience to God is likewise moved by nothing but the constancy of remembering Him, He said, after emphasizing His Prophet's ﷺ marriage to Zaynab (p-369) (may God be pleased with her), that He, glory be to Him, had married her to him because He decreed that there be no fatherhood between him and any of the men of his community that would make the wife of a son unlawful: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., who claim that with their tongues, ﴿remember﴾, i.e., in confirmation of your claim, ﴿God﴾, who is greater than every thing, ﴿with much remembrance﴾, i.e., by ascribing to Him, glory be to Him, the attributes of perfection and praising Him with them by your tongues, so that you do not forget Him in any state of affairs, so that this may move you to honor His Messenger ﷺ with its due honor, and to believe in his perfection in every state, and that he does not speak from desire, ﴿that you may obtain forgiveness and a great reward﴾, as the promise of it has already been stated.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 42:

Since the establishment of prophethood between Him and any of the men would undermine the comprehensiveness of (His) knowledge, it was necessary to declare Him, glory be to Him, free of that. So He said: ﴿And glorify Him﴾, i.e., (declare Him free) from there being anything contrary to what He has informed of, and from every attribute of deficiency, after you have affirmed for Him every attribute of perfection, ﴿in the morning and the evening﴾, i.e., at the beginning of the day and at its end, meaning constantly, because these two times are either times of preoccupation that occupies one at the start or at the end, or times of rest. Thus, the obligation of remembrance during them is an obligation of it at other times by way of a fortiori reasoning. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Allah did not impose any obligation upon His servants without setting for it a known limit."

Then, the excuse of its people in the state of excuse is other than the remembrance, for He, exalted is He, did not set a limit for it at which it ends, and He did not excuse anyone from abandoning it except one overpowered in his intellect. And these two [the remembrance and the glorification] are also witnessed by the angels and indicate the Hour. The second indicates its nearness through the passing away of the whole world, and the first indicates resurrection after death. It is possible that this refers to the two prayers of dawn and afternoon, because perseverance in them, given what was pointed to of their difficulty through the occupation with rest and other things that befall them at their times, indicates the utmost love for standing before the Lord's presences, and it moves one to persevere in the other prayers and in all acts of obedience by way of priority. This second [meaning] is confirmed by His expressing it with the word "prayer" in explaining that, His mention of it to us, glorified is He, began with His saying: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you﴾, that is, with the attribute of the All-Merciful, showing tenderness, because one of us who prays inclines with compassion in the postures. ﴿And His angels﴾, that is, all of them, [send blessings] by seeking forgiveness for you and protecting you from many sins and calamities. Some of them move back and forth between Him, glorified is He, and the prophets, through the remembrance that descends to them that guards from every evil. Thus the two prayers are shared in showing the nobility of those addressed.

And since the act of the angels [is attributed to Him], because, although He is the Creator of it and the One who commands it, He said: ﴿that He may bring you out﴾, that is, by that, ﴿from the darknesses﴾ [that is] those arising from ignorance, which necessitates misguidance, ﴿into the light﴾, that is, which arises from knowledge, which bears the fruit of guidance. So some of you come out in fact from the darknesses of sins, which necessitate the rust upon the heart, into the light of acts of obedience, and you thereby become believers. ﴿And He has been﴾, that is, from eternity and to eternity, ﴿toward the believers﴾, that is, those for whom faith has become firmly established [especially], ﴿merciful﴾, that is, abounding in mercy by granting them success in doing what the Divinity is pleased with, for they are the people of His special favor. So He moves them to sincerity in acts of obedience, and He raises their ranks in the gardens of the Paradises.

Since the most evident of the times in which the fruit of this attribute appears is what comes after death, God the Exalted said, explaining their honor: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be peace﴾, meaning, by death or by resurrection. ﴿Peace﴾, meaning they say to Him that: "You are peace, and from You is peace, so we have come to our Lord with peace" [as the muhrim says, which resembles the state of one who is in the gathering (al-hashr), so they are answered with peace], which shows their nobility and in which they are secure from every harm. ﴿And He has prepared﴾, meaning, and the state is that He has prepared ﴿for them﴾, meaning after the lasting safety, ﴿a generous reward﴾, meaning an abundant, lasting bounty in which there is no turbidity in any part of it.

When He had admonished the believers concerning him (ﷺ) in what precedes, drawing their ears and hearts toward him, and concluded with what necessitates for them success through what is with Him, glory be to Him, and since the greater part of that was addressed to him (ﷺ), for he is the head of the believers, He turned the address to him directly and directed it toward him, saying, exalting his mention and raising high his rank, with what is strung together with His saying ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39] and what follows it of reproach: ﴿O Prophet﴾ [i.e., the one whose report concerns what no one else is aware of].

(p. 372) When the disbelievers, both the openly defiant among them and those who concealed it, denied the prophethood and what follows from it, He emphasized His words concerning its matter and magnified it, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾, i.e., by Our majesty, with what We inform you of to all of Our creation, ﴿as a witness﴾, i.e., over them and in their favor, an unrestricted witnessing, because none knows the inward matters except Allah, and you are one whose testimony is accepted. So convey to them the entire message, whether that pleases them or displeases them; your act is witnessed by them, whether it pleases you or displeases you.

When the purpose was to inform of the firmness of his footing in each of these attributes, He joined them with the conjunction "and," saying: ﴿and a bearer of good tidings﴾, i.e., to those for whom you testify good, with what gladdens them. He indicated the intensification in giving good tidings by the doubling of the form (al-tad'if), because of what it has of good effect in bringing the invited one toward acceptance; and the doubling carries an indication of the multitude of the act and its object, a good tiding of the multitude of the follower, which is the cause of the aim of the surah. The intensification in warning was greater, because it is more eloquent in repelling the opponent, and it is the primary aim of the message, owing to the difficulty of daring to oppose it. So He said: ﴿and a warner﴾, [i.e.,] to those over whom you testify [with evil], with what distresses them.

﴿And as one who calls﴾, meaning to both groups, ﴿to Allah﴾, meaning to that which pleases the One than whom there is none greater, by word and deed. He left the calling unqualified by any intensifier, because it encompasses good tidings, warning, informing about stories and parables, and establishing rulings and limits. What is commanded in all of this is conveying the message according to need, with emphasis or without it. (p-373) Whoever is not turned from his error by warning, and is not brought back to his right course by good tidings, is compelled to it by the sword.

Since this is extremely difficult, and no one can carry it out except with a great help from Allah, He indicated this by His words: ﴿by His permission﴾, meaning by His enabling you to call through facilitating its means and bearing its burdens, and by enabling the one called to accept and follow, if He wills good for him.

Since the one who calls to Allah must have light, because the proofs are manifest, He said: ﴿and as a lamp﴾, which supplies insight and thus clears away the darkness of ignorance with knowledge that makes visible the places of error, just as physical light is supplied by the light of eyes. Since the context points to its illuminating, and since there are lamps that do not give light, and since explicit statement and emphasis have great importance, He said: ﴿giving light﴾, meaning it gives light to whoever follows it so that he walks in the greatest radiance, while whoever lags behind it is in the greatest darkness. [Thus it is understood from the restriction by "light" that it is the seat of the comparison, and He expressed it with "light" rather than "sun" because it borrows from it without diminishing, although "sun" is also one of its names.]

When these excellent attributes had been set forth, and the fruits of them were to be applied to them at the summit of loftiness, and the witness was the clear proof, it was as if it were said: "So establish the luminous proofs, call to Allah, and warn [every one] who opposes your command." The occasion called for addressing those who turn toward (the message), so he omitted this implied element, since it is for those who turn away, and indicated it by his words, coupled with a conjunction to it [ʿalayhi]: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, i.e., those in whom this attribute is sound. For you are a bearer of good tidings ﴿that for them there is﴾ and he clarified the greatness of this good tidings by his words: ﴿from Allah﴾, i.e., He who possesses all attributes of greatness, ﴿a great bounty﴾, i.e., in terms of its preciousness and in terms of its multiplication, from ten times the like of a good deed up to what none knows except Allah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 48:

When Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) commanded him with what gladdens him, He forbade him from what harms him. So He said, mentioning the fruit of warning: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the opponents (al-mushaqqin), ﴿and the hypocrites﴾, meaning: do not abandon conveying any part [of what You have sent down to you of revelation, and its like, out of aversion to something] of their speech or their deeds concerning the matter of Zaynab or others, for you are a warner to them. He added, beyond what was in the beginning of the surah, the point of benefit in His saying, explicitly stating what the preceding context required: ﴿And leave﴾, i.e., let go, while you remain in a good state with you and a beautiful matter for you, ﴿their harm﴾. So do not watch out for it in anything, do not take it into account at all, and be patient with it, for it will not harm you, because Allah is repelling [harm] from you, because you are one who calls to Him by His permission.

When abandoning the one who harms and turning away from him in submission was extremely difficult, He reminded him of the remedy, so He said: ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, in giving you victory over them [and] conveying all that He commands you to convey, and in all your affairs, because Allah is the one who perfects your light and makes your religion prevail. Relying on Him is among the fruits of His illuminating you by making you a lamp (siraj). And since the one entrusted (al-wakil) may not be able to undertake all matters, He said, informing that His sufficiency is all-encompassing: ﴿And sufficient is﴾, and he emphasized the matter of sufficiency by inserting the preposition bi- before the agent (fa'il), to affirm that He is the agent, as passed at the end of Surat al-Ra'd (p-375), so He said: ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the One who has complete encompassing [knowledge and power], and He made the relation specific by the agent in origin, for greater emphasis in affirming the meaning of the agent, so He said: ﴿as Disposer of affairs (wakil)﴾. Whoever is content with Him, He illuminates for him all his affairs.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 49:

When Allah, glorified is He, commanded the conveying of His commands without turning to anyone other than Him, and it was known that this requires attempts and disputes, which none undertakes except one who has turned away from the creatures because of what he witnesses of the greatness of the Creator, He commanded reliance upon Him (tawakkul), and He established the witnessed proof through the story of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and Qurayza, as sufficiency for whoever is sincere toward Him. When the proof was complete, He returned to explaining what He had opened the surah with of rulings, after repeating the command to rely upon Him. So He mentioned the closest form of divorce to the meaning of the zihar mentioned at the beginning of the surah, after the command to rely upon Him, the aim of which is that the one who made zihar should not approach her after he had nullified the zihar. So He said [forbidding those who are at the lowest rank of faith, after the good tidings to the believers], cutting them off from what they used to strive for in restricting the divorced woman, with the intent of harming her or of having full control over her: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, who claim that, ﴿when you marry﴾, meaning, contract marriage. He used the name of the effect for the cause, since it has become a technical (shar'i) meaning in it. ﴿the believing women﴾, meaning, those described with this noble attribute, which requires the utmost desire for them and completes the bond between you and them.

Since a long period of detention through the contract without intercourse does not change the ruling regarding the waiting period ('iddah), whereas for other matters such as lineage the mere possibility of intercourse suffices, and since divorce does not occur except after marriage [and after the lawfulness of intercourse through marriage], He indicated this with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾, meaning, by way of the sequence (tawzi'). It was said to Ibn 'Abbas that Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, holds the validity of attaching divorce before marriage, and he said: "A slip of scholarship," and he recited this verse.

Since the intent is the negation of touching (masis) in this marriage specifically, and not absolutely, and since the ruling for obligating the dower depends on the act of intercourse itself and not on its possibility, even if seclusion (khalwa) has occurred, He introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿before you touch them﴾, meaning, have intercourse with them. He used "touch" for intercourse because it is a means to it, just as He called wine a sin because it is its cause. Since the waiting period is a right of the men, He said: ﴿then there is not for you﴾, and since the waiting period is obligatory, He expressed it with the particle of elevation, saying: ﴿against them﴾, and He emphasized the negation by affirming the preposition in His saying: ﴿any waiting period﴾, and it indicates their habit of that, their exaggeration in it, and their harassment through it, as in zihar with the form of ifti'al, so He said: ﴿you count it﴾, meaning, you exert yourselves to count it [and] observe it. It was narrated from Ibn Kathir through the route of al-Bazzi as an anomalous reading with the lightening of the dal, meaning, you exert yourselves in transgressing against the divorced woman by means of it.

Since this ruling, whose meaning is separation, is for believing women who have attributes that require the continuance of companionship and the completeness of union, it would apply to the women of the People of the Book all the more so. The benefit of the restriction is guidance that one should not turn away from believing women, and indeed not even from the righteous among believing women. And since the discourse, as has been indicated, concerns a woman near to the one who made zihar against her, and since what is free of the obligation of a fixed dower is closer to that, He made a consequence of what preceded by His saying: ﴿so provide for them﴾, without declaring that this is for one for whom no dower was named, so that the one for whom a dower was named enters into the discourse by way of recommendation (nadb), along with her being entitled to half of the [named] dower, as the first (case) entered by way of obligation. ﴿And release them﴾, meaning, let them go so that they may leave your homes, and do not hold anything against them with a pretext, ﴿a fair release﴾, with kindness in word and deed, without any harm in any way [at all], so that he may marry whomever he wishes.

(p. 378) When the Prophet was the most entitled of the believers over themselves, and the greatest purpose of these verses was to explain what Allah honoured him with in that regard, He followed what He had explained, namely that there is no waiting period (*'iddah*) for him in marrying the believers, and what He forbade them of restricting the divorced wives, with some of what Allah the Exalted honoured him with and singled him out for, of the matter of [latitude in] marriage. He concluded it by saying that his wives may not be lawful for anyone after him. Thus they are like one whose waiting period is established and never ends, or like one whose husband is absent from her while he is alive, because the Prophet ﷺ is alive in his grave. He says: ﴿O Prophet﴾, mentioning, glorified is He, the attribute that is the source of nearness, its purpose, the wellspring of perfection, and its pivot.

When those in whose hearts is a sickness denied the distinctive qualities of the Prophet ﷺ, He emphasised His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives﴾, meaning their marriage. Al-Hirali said in his book on the foundations of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*): "Attaching a ruling to concrete things is specific to a particular meaning of them, such as: I have forbidden or made lawful the woman, meaning her marriage; the horse, meaning riding it; wine, meaning drinking it; the flesh of swine, meaning eating it; the sea, meaning sailing on it; the bull, meaning ploughing with it. Likewise, everything that is specific to its particular denotation, and it is not diverted from that except by an indicator, and there is no ambiguity in it, because specificity is preponderant." End of quotation.

When the purpose of this surah was to explain his virtues ﷺ and what Allah singled him out with, [a matter] that the hypocrites might criticise, namely that he is more entitled than anyone to himself and his wealth, He explained that, despite that, he would accept only the most perfect. So He explained that he used to hasten the bridal gifts (*mahr*) and pay the rewards in full. He said: ﴿those to whom you have given﴾, meaning by giving, which is the reality, and it is by him ﷺ that it is more fitting, or by naming it in the contract. Al-Kashshaf says: "Hastening [the payment] was the custom and practice of the early generations, and nothing else was known among them." ﴿their rewards﴾, meaning their bridal gifts, because they are a recompense for the benefit of intimacy, and the origin of *ajr* (reward) is recompense for an action. ﴿and what your right hand possesses﴾.

When a person's possession of what he has taken captive is more pleasing to himself, more elevated in rank, and more lawful than what he has bought, He said: ﴿of what Allah has restored﴾, meaning returned, ﴿to you﴾, the One to whom all command belongs, such as Safiyya bint Huyayy al-Nadriyya, Rayhana al-Quraziyya, and Juwayriyya bint al-Harith al-Khuza'iyya, may Allah be pleased with them, of what was in the hands of the disbelievers. He attributed it to Himself, glorified is He, to convey that it is spoils in the manner that Allah made lawful, with no betrayal in it. He used the expression "spoils" (*fay'*), whose meaning is "return," to convey that what is in the hand of a disbeliever does not belong to him; rather it belongs to whoever seizes it from him among the believers by force, or to whoever the disbeliever gives of them willingly. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ used to give whatever was requested of him from the lands or women of the disbelievers, and he never gave anyone anything without it reaching him, such as Tamim al-Dari and Shuwayl, may Allah be pleased with them both. He qualified it with this as an alert to his virtue ﷺ and that he attained every thing in its best form, as the allusion to this has already passed. It is also an indication that it had been foreknown in Allah's knowledge that nothing would reach him from the possession of the right hand except what was of this kind. It included what was given to him as a gift by disbelievers, such as Mariya al-Qibtiyya, the mother of his son Ibrahim, upon him be peace (*umm walad*, a slave-concubine who bore a child to her master). In this is also an indication of what he was singled out with, namely the making lawful of what was forbidden to those before him of the spoils. ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles﴾, full or otherwise, is included a fortiori, for the further the lineage, the more fitting it is to be lawful.

Since He had mentioned the paternal uncle in the singular, because the singular of males encompasses others by virtue of its nobility, its strength, and its being the origin from which this species branches, He made clear with all the females that the intended meaning is the category, lest it be supposed that the intention is the permissibility of sisters gathered together. So He said: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, from the women of the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib.

Since He began with the paternal uncles for their nobility, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles﴾, also proceeding in singular and plural in that manner: ﴿and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, meaning from the women of the Banu Zuhra. [It is possible that there is a wonderful interweaving in this, namely: the daughters of your paternal uncle and the daughters of your uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunt and the daughters of your paternal aunt, the daughters of your maternal uncle and the daughters of your maternal uncles, the daughters of your maternal aunt and the daughters of your maternal aunt; and its secret is what has been pointed out.]

Since He had explained the nobility of his wives from the aspect of lineage, because it is known and well established that the lineage of the Prophet ﷺ, both from the men's and the women's side, is the noblest of lineages, to the extent that no two Arabs differ regarding this, He explained their nobility from the aspect of deeds. So He said: (p. 381) ﴿who emigrated﴾, and by His saying ﴿with you﴾ He indicated that the emigration was before the conquest [of Mecca]: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. He did not intend by this a restriction, but an alert to their nobility, and an indication that it had been foreknown in His knowledge, glorified is He, that he would never marry anyone who lacked these qualities. It has been reported that this is by way of restriction. Al-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, al-Tabarani, al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim all narrated it, all through al-Suddi from Abu Salih from Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to me, and I excused myself [to him], and he accepted my excuse. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives﴾, the verse. So I was not lawful for him, because I had not emigrated. I was of the freed captives (*tulaqa'*)." Al-Tirmidhi said: "A good hadith, which we only know through this chain, from the hadith of al-Suddi."

Since He had explained what is most noble of marriage, because it is the origin, He followed it, glorified is He, with what His law singled him out with of the spoils, which He Himself undertook to make lawful. He followed it with what its permissibility came from the side of the one granting permission, to inform that it is not of the type of charity from which He had exalted his rank. So He said: ﴿and a woman﴾, meaning and We have made lawful to you a woman ﴿who is a believer﴾, meaning of this category, whether free or enslaved, ﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾.

When He mentioned the attribute of prophethood, because it is the pivot of honour from the Creator and of love from the creatures (p. 382), honouring him with it and attaching the ruling to the attribute: for if He had said "for you," it might have occurred to some minds, as al-Zajjaj said, that it is not specific to him ﷺ. He repeated it as an explanation of the greater nobility he has, in a context that removes what might be supposed, namely that it would be obligatory for him to accept. So He said: ﴿if the Prophet wishes﴾, meaning the one whose rank We have exalted by what We have singled him out with of informing about great matters from the unseen and the seen realms, ﴿to take her in marriage﴾, meaning to bring about his marriage to her, making her one of his wives, by a contract or by possession of the right hand, so that she becomes his alone without a bridal gift, without a guardian, and without witnesses.

Since it might be understood that others share with him in this meaning, He said, explaining the particularity and describing the verbal noun: ﴿We have made lawful﴾, magnifying the matter with the intensive particle, turning to direct address because it specifies the intended meaning and removes doubt: ﴿exclusively for you﴾. He increased the meaning in clarity with His saying: ﴿apart from the believers﴾, meaning apart from the prophets and others. He used the unrestricted description that conveys firmness, so it includes whoever is qualified by excellence and certainty, and other colours; it includes, a fortiori, those who fall below their rank among the believers (alladhina yu'minun) and those who have believed (alladhina amanu) and all other people, by way of the understanding of agreement. The women who gave themselves were a number, and he had none of them. Al-Bukhari narrated from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "I used to be jealous of those who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (p. 383), and I would say: Is a woman not ashamed to give herself? When there was revealed: ﴿You may put off whom you wish of them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51], I said: O Messenger of Allah, I see that your Lord only hastens to fulfil your desire."

Since specification is not valid nor conceivable except from comprehensive knowledge that this matter was not for anyone other than the one specified, with full power, so as to prevent others from it, He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿Indeed﴾, meaning We have informed you that this is a matter that is exclusive to you over them, because ﴿We have known what We have ordained﴾, meaning what We have decreed by Our majesty.

Since what He decreed for the human being is a gift, and what We withhold is necessarily from him, He expressed it with the particle of elevation, saying: ﴿upon them﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿concerning their wives﴾, meaning that it is not lawful for them to have a woman by the wording of gift from her, nor without a bridal gift, nor without a guardian and witnesses. This is general for all believers, the earlier and the later. Since this is general to the free and the enslaved, He said: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾, meaning that no one other than you possesses an enslaved woman by her giving herself to him, so that he would have more right to her than her master.

When He had finished explaining the inferiority, He explained the specification by the figure of *laff wa-nashr* (folding and unfolding), confusedly, with His saying: ﴿so that there is no hardship upon you﴾, meaning no narrowness in any matter concerning women, since We have made lawful to you kinds of wives and increased you with the one who gives herself. When He, glorified is He, mentioned what He had ordained concerning wives and slave-women, which encompasses justice in their companionship, and the Prophet ﷺ was the most understanding of people and the most fearful of Allah among them (p. 384), and he used to be just among them, yet he would apologise, along with that, for the inclination of the heart, which is beyond the capacity of humans, by saying: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what I do not possess." He lightened it for him, glorified is He, with His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾, meaning the One characterised by the attributes of perfection, of forbearance, deliberation, power and others, from eternity to eternity, ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning of far-reaching concealment. So if He wills, He leaves off the reckoning for what He has the right to reckon him for, and in place of the reckoning He sets a great honour, characterised by that from eternity to eternity.

When he had mentioned these two attributes, he followed them with what He lifted from him concerning their affairs, as an honor to him (ﷺ), from what was part of his circumstances that he would have to bear and would find difficult to act upon. So He said, in a position of resumption (isti'naf), or as a circumstantial clause (hal) related to the meaning of the lightening (takhfif) in the preceding sentences: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them﴾, with the hamza according to the reading of the majority (al-jama'ah), meaning you postpone, ﴿whom you will of them﴾, meaning of those who offer themselves in marriage (al-wahibat), so that you do not accept their gift, or of your wives by divorce or otherwise, together with what comforts them of taking them in (an tu'wiya-hunna). Without the hamza, according to Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs, it is from hope (raja'), meaning you postpone her while doing things by which she will be hoping for your inclination. ﴿And you may take to yourself whom you will﴾, meaning you draw near and bring close, by accepting the gift, or by keeping her in the marriage bond, whether with a turn (qasm) or without a turn, with intercourse or without intercourse, singling him out with this over the rest of men. ﴿And whomever you will﴾ (p-385). The occasion of revelation of this verse was that when the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir) was revealed, they feared that he would divorce them, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah! Grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state," and so it was revealed.

Since he might sometimes incline toward the one he had separated from, the Exalted explained her ruling, saying: ﴿And whoever you seek﴾, meaning your soul inclines to seeking her, ﴿from among those you have set aside﴾, meaning you have set her aside by divorce or by returning a gift, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning in taking her in after that, by accepting her gift or by returning her to the standing she had with you, from the bond of marriage or from the turn.

Since separation as such, especially if her separation was for what was understood from her of a dislike that is suspected of her, might lead one to think that she dislikes return, He, glorified be He, informed that his wives (ﷺ) are, [unlike that], so He said: ﴿That﴾, meaning the permission granted to you from Allah and the taking in, which is of great rank, because of the nobility you possess, ﴿is more suitable﴾, meaning closer to, than the deferral and than the non-explicit mention of permission in the inimitable Qur'an, ﴿that their eyes may be comforted﴾, meaning by what they attained of your noble companionship. This is a metaphor (kinayah) for joy and tranquility at attaining the desired end, because whoever is like this, his eye is at rest, and whoever is grieved, his eye is much in motion from what he fears. This is if it is from qarar in the sense of calm; it may also be from qurr, which is the opposite of heat, because the one who is delighted has a cool eye, and the one who is grieved has a hot eye; for this reason it is said to a friend: "May Allah cool your eye," and to an enemy: "May Allah heat your eye." ﴿And they will not grieve﴾, meaning by separation or other things that cause grief. ﴿And they will be pleased﴾, knowing that this is from Allah, because of the inimitability of the speech, ﴿with what you have given them﴾, meaning of rewards and other things, such as maintenance, turn, preference and the rest.

Since emphasis (ta'kid) falls more firmly upon the soul and removes doubt, and since this was a strange matter because of its remoteness from natural dispositions, He emphasized, saying: ﴿all of them﴾, meaning not one of them except that she is likewise desiring you and content with your companionship, whether you take her in or defer her, because of your goodness of companionship, nobility of character, excellent qualities and fine conduct. And if you choose to separate from her, you know that this is a binding command from Allah; so that is less grieving for her, and thus closer to the comfort of her eye in this respect. He increased this emphasis for the strangeness of the matter, which can hardly be believed, with his saying, [in conjunction with a similar phrase: "Allah knows what is in their hearts"]: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning with His encompassing of the attributes of perfection, ﴿knows﴾, meaning with continuous knowledge, since it is related to ﴿what is in your hearts﴾, [meaning] O creatures, all of you, so there is no wonder if He knows what is in the hearts of these women.

When He, glorified be He, encouraged him to be good to them by continuing the companionship, with what He informed him of their affection for that, because he (ﷺ) was intensely fond of bringing joy into hearts, He increased the encouragement with His saying: ﴿And Allah has always been﴾, meaning eternally and forever, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, meaning of everything, of whoever obeys Him and whoever disobeys Him, ﴿Forbearing﴾, not hastening to punish whoever disobeys Him, rather continuing His goodness toward him in this world. So it is necessary to fear Him for His knowledge and to be shy before Him for His forbearance: His knowledge requires fear of Him, and His forbearance requires shame before Him. The seizure of the Forbearing is severe, so it is fitting for His servant who loves Him to be forbearing toward whoever he knows falls short in his right, for He, glorified be He, will reward him for that by being forbearing toward him in what He knows of him, and by raising his station and exalting his name. Al-Bukhari related in the Tafsir from Mu'adhah, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek permission for the day of whichever wife of ours, after this verse was revealed: "You may defer whom you will of them." I said to her: "What were you saying?" She said: "I used to say to him: If that is up to me, then I do not wish, O Messenger of Allah, to prefer anyone over you."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 52:

When He had commanded him with what is difficult, namely the change of customary practices regarding the matter of the waiting period ('iddah), and then with what may be difficult for him, peace and blessings be upon him, namely restricting him to what was mentioned, out of fear of criticism from some whose faith had not yet taken firm root, and He concluded with what gladdens his wives, He joined to it what increases their joy, namely the prohibition of others than them for him, in gratitude to them for their turning away from the world (p-388) and their choosing God and His Messenger. So He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take women [in marriage] after this﴾. And since He, exalted is He, was intensely solicitous toward him, peace and blessings be upon him, He hinted to him in the verse of prohibition that He would abrogate it for him. So He affirmed the adverbial phrase, saying: ﴿after this﴾, meaning after those nine who are with you, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said in one narration from him, as a thanksgiving from Allah to them, because when the verse of choice was revealed they chose Allah and His Messenger. Thus the verse would be abrogated by something preceding it in the arrangement (nazm) but coming after it in revelation (inzal), namely the verse ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50]. In another narration, the meaning of "after this" is "after those whom We have made lawful to you," with the attribute mentioned earlier, namely the daughters of paternal uncles and those with them. This is supported by the narration transmitted earlier from Umm Hani', may Allah be pleased with her.

Since he might have understood that the intended restriction is to the number nine, without the condition of those specific persons, He said: ﴿nor that you exchange them﴾, meaning these nine, and He emphasized the negation with His words ﴿any﴾, meaning anything of ﴿wives﴾, that is, by divorcing some of these specific persons and taking in their place others from among other women through a marriage contract, in such a way that the number does not exceed nine. From this it is known that what is forbidden is marrying others while divorcing one of them first. This supports the first narration from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, because the one who is exchanged for must be known in person. As for the reply to the statement of Umm Hani' (p-389), may Allah be pleased with her, it is that he understood it from her, not a narration from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And when one of them dies, there is no blame in marrying one in her place.

Since it is known from this that the prohibition applies to every wife, of whatever description she may be, He confirmed the meaning and established it, and stated it explicitly in His words as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of "exchange": ﴿even if her beauty pleases you﴾, meaning, women other than those who are with you. In this is the permission to look at the one who is intended for marriage, because a first glance hardly establishes the true attributes of the one looked at. And since the word "women" includes wives and female slaves, He clarified that the intended meaning is wives [only] by His words: ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning that for you there is lawful from them whatever you wish. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, possessed Rayhana, may Allah be pleased with her, from the captives of Banu Qurayza, and she remained in his possession for a period during which he did not approach her until she embraced Islam. Then, after the year of al-Hudaybiyya, he possessed Mariya, may Allah be pleased with her, the mother of his son Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

When He, glorified is He, had preceded in these verses with commands, prohibitions, and the setting of limits, He warned against negligence regarding any of them, even under some form of interpretation, and said: ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful﴾, meaning, He than whom nothing is greater, who encompasses all attributes of perfection. ﴿Over all things watchful﴾ means He acts as one who watches over what may be exposed to defect at the closest proximity to it, such that nothing of the matter being watched over is lost under His watch, (p-390) and a watcher is none but near, and none is nearer than the nearness of the Truth, glorified is He. So He does not neglect whom He watches, and this is among the most severe of the names in terms of warning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar, *Nazm al-Durar fi Tanasub al-Ayat wa al-Suwar*) on surah 33, verse 53 (part 1 of 2):

Since nearness and encompassing belong to Allah, in reality there is no watcher except Him. The verse, in any case, is abrogated (*mansukhah*) if we take either of the first two possibilities. al-Tirmidhi related in his *Tafsir* from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and how could she not be, especially in this field, that she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until Allah made wives lawful for him." He said: "This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth." End of quote. Ibn al-Jawzi transmitted from her, may Allah be pleased with her, that the abrogating verse (*al-nasikh*) is ﴿We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50]. Likewise, from a group of them: ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with them all. However, he (ﷺ) left that alone out of courtesy toward Allah the Exalted, since he expressed the prohibition in the form of a statement and the imperfect verb, and out of consideration for their rights, which Allah indicated by their being given the choice of the Hereafter.

When he (ﷺ) confined it to them, and he had previously instructed them to remain in their houses and to abandon the ostentatious display (*tabarruj*) of the Age of Ignorance, he lowered the veil (*ḥijab*) over them within the houses and prohibited others besides him (ﷺ) from what the Arabs used to do, namely entering upon women, because of the trust (*amanah*) they held regarding this matter. So he said (p. 391), addressing the lowest tier of the people of this religion, because of what was mentioned about the cause of its revelation, and because the believers were refraining from this without anyone forbidding them, as is indicated by what will come from ʿUmar's statement, may Allah be pleased with him, about the veil. ﴿O you who believe﴾ means: you who claim faith. Let your claim be true. ﴿Do not enter﴾ together in a group. So the individual is included a fortiori.

Since the disturbance of the mind may at times distract one from something Allah informs him of, as indicated by his (ﷺ) saying: "The Night of Power was shown to me, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, and so it was made to slip from me," or as he (ﷺ) said, he expressed it with the attribute of prophethood in His saying: ﴿the houses of the Prophet﴾, meaning the one to whom news comes from the Knower of the unseen, which is of the utmost loftiness, in any circumstance at all. ﴿Unless﴾, in the case that ﴿you are given permission﴾, meaning by one who has the authority to grant permission in his (ﷺ) houses, from him or from one whom he authorizes to do so, ﴿going in for a meal﴾, meaning for eating it, while ﴿not waiting for its preparation﴾, meaning waiting for the time of that meal, its readiness, and its being ready to be eaten. By this he forbade those who would watch for the meal of the Prophet (ﷺ), because that would burden him (ﷺ) greatly, for there may be someone there who needs that meal more than the one waiting for it, or other excuses. So the address (p. 392) does not apply to anyone other than the lowest tier. Whoever slips from a higher rank is included in their address, according to the rank that has been brought down to him. The use of the bare active participle in ﴿waiting﴾ (*nāẓirīn*) is more emphatic in the prohibition.

Since this entering with permission was absolute, and it was intended to be restricted, and the original form of that would have been: "If you are invited..." and so on, but because the context called for a definitive conclusion regarding what is mentioned, and because the *istidrāk* (the corrective contrast) carries a great effect of stirring and shaking the soul, by informing it that what follows contradicts what precedes, he said: ﴿But when you are invited﴾, meaning by one who has the authority to invite, ﴿then enter﴾, meaning for the sake of what he invited you to. Then he made the following a consequence of this: ﴿and when you have eaten﴾, meaning you have eaten food or drunk a drink, ﴿then disperse﴾, meaning go wherever you wish at once, and do not linger after the meal, neither resting while the food settles in your bellies, ﴿nor seeking familiar conversation﴾, meaning seeking intimacy for its sake. Hamzah ibn Nadr al-Kirmani said in his book *Jawami' al-Tafsir*: al-Hasan said: "It is enough of a condemnation of the burdensome that Allah did not make an allowance for them in this matter." End of quote. And from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "It is enough of a condemnation of the burdensome that Allah did not tolerate them." Then he gave the reason for that in His saying, directing the address to all of them and magnifying it with the distal demonstrative: ﴿Indeed, that﴾, meaning the matter that is severe (p. 393), namely remaining after finishing eating and drinking, ﴿was troubling the Prophet﴾, meaning the one whom We prepared to hear what We inform him of, which would be the cause of your honor and elevation in both abodes. So beware of occupying him from anything of that, lest We inform him of something through which you perish.

Then, on account of that prohibition, he made the following a cause for what removes his hurt, by preventing them from confronting him with it. He said: ﴿so he is shy﴾, meaning shyness exists, and its root is the bringing about of life, as if whoever has no shyness is lifeless, having no life, ﴿of you﴾, meaning [shy] to tell you to leave. ﴿But Allah﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs all command, ﴿is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning He does not act as one who is shy, which would lead Him to abandon commanding it.

Since the house (*al-bayt*) is used for the woman because she habitually remains in it, he returned the pronoun to it, intending by it the women, as a figure of speech (*istikhdam*). So he said: ﴿And when you ask of them﴾, meaning the wives, ﴿something of goods﴾, meaning an item of household utensils, ﴿then ask them﴾, meaning that goods, while being ﴿from behind a screen (*ḥijāb*)﴾, meaning a curtain that conceals you from them and conceals them from you. ﴿That﴾, meaning the matter of high rank which I inform you all of, namely asking from behind a screen and other things, ﴿is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, meaning [from] the whisperings of Satan, which he used to whisper in the days of ignorance, being content with what they were in the snare of, namely polytheism. ﴿And it is not for you﴾, meaning it is not proper, nor fitting in any circumstance, ﴿to harm﴾, and He mentioned them by the attribute that is the cause of their happiness (p. 394), and by which they deserve from Him a right they cannot fulfill by giving thanks for it. So He said: ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾ (ﷺ), meaning the one who possesses all perfection, so he has from you a kindness that deserves from you the utmost honor and reverence, let alone refraining from harm. So do not harm him by entering any of his houses without his permission, or by remaining after the need has been fulfilled, nor by anything else.

Since he (ﷺ) had confined them to himself, and it was necessary, after he had made others lawful for him, that he confine them to himself after death, as an increase in his honor and a display of his distinction, he said: ﴿And never to marry his wives after him﴾, meaning in the time to come, ﴿after his passing﴾, meaning after his separation from those with whom he had consummated marriage, whether by death or divorce, because it has preceded that he is alive and has not died, ﴿ever﴾. For the waiting period (*ʿiddah*) from him ought not to end, because of his greatness, majesty, and perfection, and he is alive in his grave, ever. [There is another cause more general than this, which is touched upon in the matter of inheritance, namely cutting off desires from extending to anything of this world after him, lest anyone wish for his (ﷺ) death in order to take that, and thereby disbelieve, for there is no faith for one who does not prefer him over himself.] As for al-ʿĀliyah bint Ẓabyan, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) divorced and who then married someone else, her matter was before the revelation of this verse. This was mentioned by al-Baghawi from Maʿmar from al-Zuhri. Then he gave the reason for that in His saying: ﴿Indeed, that﴾, meaning harming him by marriage and other things, which should be (p. 395) at the utmost remove, ﴿was in the sight of Allah﴾, meaning the One Capable of everything, ﴿tremendous﴾.

Many things have been reported regarding the cause of revelation of this verse. Abu Yaʿla al-Mawsili related in his *Musnad* from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Umm Sulaym, may Allah be pleased with her, sent me with fresh dates to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a tray, at the first ripening of the date-palm fruit. He said: I entered upon him, placed it before him, and he ate from it. Then he took me by the hand and we went out. It was recent since the wedding of Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her. He said: He passed by some of his wives, with men sitting with them conversing, and they congratulated him, and the people congratulated him. They said: 'Praise be to Allah who has brought comfort to your eye, O Messenger of Allah.' He went on until he came to ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and there were men with her. He said: He disliked that, and whenever he disliked something it was recognized in his face. He said: I came to Umm Sulaym and informed her. Abu Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'If what your son said is [true], something will happen.' He said: When it was evening, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, ascended the pulpit, then recited this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission﴾, the verse. He said: And he commanded the veil." Its origin in *Tafsir* is from the *Jami'* of al-Tirmidhi. Al-Bukhari and others related from him, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was a bridegroom to Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, and Umm Sulaym said to me: 'If only we would send a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ)' (p. 396). I said to her: 'Do it.' So she made for it dates, *aqit* (dried curd), and ghee, and prepared a *hays* (a dish of dates, curd, and ghee) in a cooking pot, and she sent it with me to him. He said to me: 'Put it down.' Then he commanded me and said: 'Call for me men,' and he named them, 'and call for me whoever you meet.' I did what he commanded, then I returned and the house was overflowing with its people." In al-Tirmidhi's narration, the narrator said: "I said to Anas: 'How many were they?' He said: 'About three hundred.'" He said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) place his hand upon that *hays*, speak what Allah willed, and then began to call them ten by ten, and they ate from it, and he would say to them: 'Mention the name of Allah, and let each man eat from what is in front of him,' until they all dispersed from it." al-Tirmidhi said: "He said to me, 'O Anas, lift up!' So I lifted, and I do not know whether it was more when I placed it or when I lifted it. Some of them left, and a group remained conversing." He said: "And I began to be distressed." al-Tirmidhi said: "The Messenger of Allah was sitting, and his wife had turned her face toward the wall, and they were burdensome to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." ʿAbd al-Razzaq said in his *Tafsir*: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to be shy of them, not to say anything to them." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out toward the apartments, and I went out following him, and I said: 'They have gone.' He returned, entered the house, and let down the curtain, and I was in the apartment while he was saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission﴾, the verse." In al-Tirmidhi's narration: "Then he returned. When they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returning, they thought they had been burdensome to him, so they hurried to the door and all went out. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came until he let down the curtain and entered while I was sitting in the apartment. He did not remain but a little until he came out to me, and these verses were revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and recited them to the people: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾, the verse." [And] al-Shaykhan and others related from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and this is the wording of al-Bukhari, in narrations: "The Prophet (ﷺ) consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh with bread and meat. She sent out a summoner to the food, so people came, ate, and left, then other people came, ate, and left. So I summoned until I could find no one to summon. I said: 'O Prophet of Allah! I cannot find anyone to summon.' He said: 'Lift your food.' They sat conversing in the house, and he appeared as though preparing to stand, but they did not stand. When he saw that, he stood, and when he stood, whoever stood stood, and three persons remained seated." In another narration: "Three men. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out and set off to the apartment of ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: 'Peace be upon you, people of the house, and the mercy of Allah.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) went on. "She said: 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah. How did you find your family? May Allah bless you!'" Then he went around to the chambers of all his wives, saying to each of them what he had said to A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and they replied to him as A'ishah had replied. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned, and behold, the people were still sitting. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely shy, so he went out, heading toward the chamber of A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her).

And in another narration: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held a wedding feast (walimah) when he married Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her). He fed the people bread and meat. Then he went out to the chambers of the Mothers of the Believers, as he used to do on the morning after his marriage. He would greet them and supplicate for them, and they would greet him and supplicate for him. When he returned to his house, he saw two men engaged in conversation. When he saw them, he turned back from his house. When the two men saw the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), they turned back from his house and rose hastily. I do not know whether I informed him of their departure or he was informed that the people had left. So he returned until, when he had placed one foot on the threshold of the door, inside, and the other outside, he let down the curtain." In another narration: "I went to enter, and he cast the screen (hijab) between me and him, and the verse of the hijab was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ [33:53]."

Al-Bukhari also narrates from A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) who said: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Veil your wives.' She said: 'But he did not do so. The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go out at night to the open area (al-manasi') beyond the settlement. Sawdah bint Zam'ah, who was a tall woman (may Allah be pleased with her), went out, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) saw her while he was in a gathering and said: 'I recognized you, O Sawdah,' out of eagerness that the veil would be revealed.' She said: 'So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the veil.'"

Al-Bukhari from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), and Muslim from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), both from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Your wives are entered upon by the righteous and the wicked. If only you would order them to veil themselves.' Then the verse of the hijab was revealed."

Other occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) have been related besides these, and it has already been established that it is no innovation for a single verse to have several occasions of revelation of equal rank, or some closer than others. However, al-Bukhari, in his Tafsir, in the context of this verse, related something explicit that the story of Sawdah occurred after the veil, from A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Sawdah went out after the hijab had been imposed, for some need of hers. She was a large woman who was not hidden from anyone who knew her. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) saw her and said: 'O Sawdah! By Allah, you are not concealed from us. So consider how you go out.' She said: 'So she turned back, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house having his evening meal, and in his hand was a bone (irq). She entered and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I went out for some need of mine, and 'Umar said to me such and such.' She said: 'Then Allah revealed to him, and then it was lifted from him, while the bone was still in his hand, not yet put down. He said: 'Permission has been given to you that you may go out for your needs.'"

As for those who sat [in the house], while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in the state of disliking their sitting, as described in his condition through his shyness and his preparation to rise and the like, they did not derive jurisprudence (fiqh) from his states. Rather, they stopped at what they heard from his speech. The way of the perfected ones (al-kummal) is to gain insight from his outward form (rasm) and state (hal), just as they gain insight from his speech and deeds. Al-Hirali said: "The state (hal) is every appearance that arises from an inner emotion (infi'al batin), and understanding it is specific to the observer who discerns (al-mutawassim). Such is his (ﷺ) laughing at the man whom he saw on the day of Khaybar, who had taken a bag of fat from the spoils (fay') of the Jews and was saying: 'I will not give anyone any of this today.' Likewise, the change in his face toward 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) when he began reading to him a sheet of the wisdom of the ancients, until the one who discerned the Prophet's (ﷺ) disapproval of 'Umar's action in his face alerted 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). The informing of every state (hal) from these is by reckoning what the emotion indicates of expansion, contraction, aversion, and the like, which the discerning one perceives, and which the understanding one is certain of by its requirement. As for the outward form (rasm), it is everything whose nature is to remain after his absence and his death, so the one who reflects derives from it the ruling of its placement and the purpose of its form. Such as what is seen of the form of his building of his mosque in a state of making do with the easiest possible means, and his building of his houses in a form without ostentation, and without excess beyond the need. And like the woolen cloak (kisa' mulabbad) that he left, and his bed, and the like of the furnishings of his houses. And as one understands from his care for the instruments of his weapons, such as his sword being adorned with silver and its hilt being silver, and like his care for perfume, to the extent that it was seen on his garment and his collar. Thus one learns from his outward forms his rulings, just as one learns from his states, deeds, and sayings. This is because all these manifestations are in reality what speech is." End of quotation.

The proof of this is that the origin of everything is inner speech (al-kalam al-nafsi), which is the source, while speech, action, state, and outward form are translations of it. None of them is more deserving of being a translation than another. Yes, some of them are more indicative than others, more explicit and clearer. So the Prophet's (ﷺ) preparation to rise from his house is like if he had said: "I want you to leave." For a man's rising from his house, which is the place that conceals him from others, necessarily means that he wants others to depart, so that they do not witness what he does not wish anyone to witness. And his coming in order to enter, then, upon seeing them, turning back, is like if he had said: "What prevents me from entering the place of my rest is your sitting in it, because of the burden of your sitting upon me." And likewise the states and the outward forms. And Allah is the Guide.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 54:

Since some of what indicates speech is, as has passed, more explicit than others, a person may conceal an intention to do harm when he is able to do it, and he may harm someone through an action he performs while claiming that he intended something else that does not harm. So God, the Exalted, said, urging them to be alert and attentive in words and other things, and in intentions, both good ones outwardly and inwardly, in the form of a resumption in answer to one who may have ended with his outward display while he is resolved to commit harm when he is able: ﴿Whether you disclose something or conceal it﴾, that is, with your tongues or otherwise, ﴿something﴾ [that is], of that and other than it, ﴿or conceal it﴾, that is, within your breasts.

Since the act of one who hides a matter from people is the act of one who thinks it is hidden from his Lord, He said, emphasizing it as an alert to the doer of this to this implication of his act, as a warning to him: ﴿indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection, ﴿is ever﴾ eternally and everlastingly, ﴿Knowing of all things﴾, that is, of that and other than it. ﴿He knows what you reveal and what you conceal, even if you exert yourselves in hiding it, and He will recompense you for it with reward or punishment.

(p-403) Since, as was previously mentioned, the purpose is to intensify the veil for the women who are secluded (*dhawat al-khudur*), and since [this surah] has mentioned distinctive provisions and changes of rulings for the Prophet (ﷺ), for his wives (may Allah be pleased with them), and for others, one might think that the veil, or some part of it, had changed with regard to entering [homes] or otherwise. So He excepted those whom the earlier prohibition on entering had covered in a manner that encompasses all women, as was previously stated in Surah al-Nur. He said: ﴿There is no blame﴾, that is, no sin, ﴿upon them regarding their fathers﴾, [meaning] entering and being alone [with them] without a veil. The paternal uncle, the maternal uncle, and the father-in-law are, since the spouses are considered one entity, in the position of a father. ﴿Nor their sons﴾, that is, from their own loins or by fosterage, and the son of the husband is in the position of a son. Leaving out their mention indicates that the scrupulous course is to veil from them. ﴿Nor their brothers﴾, because their shame is their shame. ﴿Nor the sons of their brothers﴾, for they are in the position of their fathers. ﴿Nor the sons of their sisters﴾, for they are in the position of their mothers. ﴿Nor their women﴾, that is, the Muslim women, whether near or distant, are of one rank. As for non-Muslim women, they are in the position of non-related men. ﴿Nor what their right hands possess﴾, because, given the authority they have over them, the suspicion of [such men] is removed out of reverence for them, along with the hardship of veiling from them.

Since suspicion is not definitively negated, and since it comes more from the women's side, for hardly does a man approach [a woman] except one he thinks will respond, because of what he sees of her signs or the signs of her appearance, He turned to address them directly, because that has a stronger impact on the soul. He said, commanding and linking to what is implied: "So display [yourselves] before whomever you wish of these": ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, the One above whom there is nothing greater, so do not approach anything that displeases Him. He omitted what the command to piety was connected to, after He had stated the negation of blame in the third-person style, and He brought out the command to piety and placed it in the second-person style, signaling that scrupulousness means not appearing before anyone other than one who has the right to enjoy [her]. If need arises, then with appearance there must be a dense veil of modesty and complete courtesy.

Since fear is only truly magnified in one who is always present, He said, giving the reason and emphasizing, as an alert that the conduct of one who is lax regarding any of His commands is the conduct of one who does not fear [Allah]; and one who does not fear is like one who thinks that He, glorified is He, does not see him: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the Mighty in station, ﴿is ever﴾ eternally and everlastingly ﴿Knowing of all things﴾ of your deeds and other things. For greater caution and scrupulousness in this matter, He expressed [it] with His words: ﴿Witness﴾, that is, nothing escapes Him, however subtle. So He observes you in private, [as with] those mentioned, just as He observes [everything] else. So let everyone beware of Him in private as they beware of Him in public. How magnificent is this overwhelming greatness, and this manifest, subduing might, which makes it right for everyone to weep blood, not merely tears, and which should deprive him of restful settlement and sweet sleep.

Al-Bukhari related from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Aflah, the brother of Abu al-Qu'ays (may Allah be pleased with him), asked permission to enter upon me after the veil had been revealed. I said: 'I will not permit him until I ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about it, for his brother Abu al-Qu'ays is not the one who nursed me; rather, the wife of Abu al-Qu'ays nursed me.' [Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon me, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Aflah, the brother of Abu al-Qu'ays, asked permission, and I refused to let him in until I asked you.'] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What prevents you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! The man is not the one who nursed me; rather, the wife of Abu al-Qu'ays nursed me.' He said: 'Let him in, for he is your paternal uncle, may your right hand be dust-covered.'" ʿUrwah said: "For this reason, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) used to say: 'Make unlawful through fosterage what you make unlawful through lineage.'"

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 56:

Since these verses, and those before and after them, are concerned with showing the nobility of the Prophet (ﷺ) and explaining his virtues, the commands, prohibitions and other rulings in them are given a reason in His saying, emphasizing that the situation requires this. As for the one who offended him by sitting beyond the appropriate time, it is clear. As for others, it was their duty not to leave the gathering until they knew who did not know proper conduct. Their laxity in this matter was the act of one who does not want to show his nobility (ﷺ). So it is discipline and warning: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ (p. 406), meaning, while you know that He possesses the attributes of greatness, majesty and might, ﴿and His angels﴾, meaning, and they are the people of purity, nearness and protection from sin.

Since He, glorified is He, had mentioned His saying, ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43], giving each a separate report, and since the Prophet (ﷺ) was the highest of those addressed in share of this, for he is the head of the believers, He singled him out here with this blessing, in which He joined the noble angels with Himself, and made the report about them a single report to make it more complete. For your saying, "So-and-so and so-and-so support so-and-so," is more emphatic than your saying, "So-and-so supports him, and so-and-so." So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They send blessings upon the Prophet﴾, meaning, they make manifest his nobility and his connection to the Greatest King, through what Allah reveals to him of the wondrous creation and command from the realm of the unseen and the witnessed. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, as narrated by al-Bukhari: "They bless him."

Since the fruit of the purpose of this information is following him (al-ta'assi), it is known from the end of the speech that the meaning is: and they greet him with peace, because that is part of the completion of the connection on which the meaning of prayer (al-salah) revolves. So this definitively yields the explanation of the intended meaning of "they send blessings": ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, who claimed this with their tongues, ﴿send blessings upon him﴾ by not being heedless of hastening to show (p. 407) his nobility at any time, confirming your claim, and because when a great person does something, every lover of his who believes in his greatness hastens to do it too, ﴿and greet him with peace﴾.

Since the purpose of both the blessing (al-salah) and the peace (al-salam) is showing nobility, and since peace is the more manifest in meaning in this, and since greeting him upon meeting is obligatory in the tashahhud without disagreement, and indicates submission to all his commands, which faith is not achieved without, and this comes from the Muslim himself, whereas blessing is what the one praying asks from Allah, He emphasized both with it, saying: ﴿with peace (taslim)﴾, meaning, so show his nobility with everything your ability reaches of good following of him, abundant good praise of him, and obedience to his command in all that he commands, and among that is sending blessings and peace upon him with your tongues, in [the manner of] what He taught you in the tashahhud and other than it, of what is reported in the hadiths from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah and others, may Allah be pleased with them. This explains the meeting of blessing and peace in showing nobility. For blessing, as [said] in al-Qamus (the lexicon al-Qamus al-Muhit), is supplication, mercy, seeking forgiveness, good praise from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and worship containing bowing and prostration. End of quote. And peace is greeting (al-tahiyyah), and greeting, as al-Baydawi (his commentary on surah al-Nisa') said, is in origin a verbal noun from "hayyaka Allah" (may Allah give you life), used as informing of life, then used for the wish and supplication with that, then it was applied to every supplication, and it became predominant in peace. In al-Qamus: greeting is peace, remaining, and dominion, and "hayyaka Allah" (p. 408) means may Allah keep you alive or make you a ruler. Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said in his Jami': peace (al-salam) is one of the names of Allah, and peace here means safety (al-salamah), as one says al-radda'and al-ridad'ah, al-ladhadh and al-ladhadhah. They said: the meaning of the speaker's saying to his companion, "Salam 'alayka," is: you are safe from me, I will not harm you with hand or tongue. It was said: its meaning is safety from Allah upon you. It was said: it is mercy. It was said: it is security. And safety is deliverance from calamities. End of quote. It has become clear that the meaning of all of them, as you see, looks at showing nobility in the manner of the necessary (malzum) looking at the necessitated (lazim). For this reason al-Baydawi explained "yusallun" with his saying: they take care to show his nobility and magnify his station, and "sallimu" with his saying: say, "al-salamu 'alayka," or submit to his commands.
