So when these two agreed in this meaning, and this was what was intended, He emphasized with the word peace to achieve the complete purpose by its indication of submission. So it is an emphasis for "salluu" in its meaning and for "sallimu" in its wording, using a term in both its literal and figurative senses, as is the position of our Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, and he gave the example of the verse of al-Nisa':

﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa': 43], and with His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾ [al-Nisa': 43], and other than that. I have explained in surah al-Ra'd that the root "salluu" in all its constructions revolves around connection, and this is necessary for everything mentioned of its interpretations. Moreover, you may make it part of al-ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis, where each of two parallel terms omits what the other expresses), so you say: the emphasis was omitted first for the verb of blessing because of what it indicates of emphasis by the verbal noun of peace, and the manifest mention of the verbal noun of peace is preferred by what has been mentioned before, and the object of peace was omitted because the object of blessing indicates it, "upon him (ﷺ)," and so that it may be suitable to be "upon him" and "for him." So it is appropriate to make surrender (al-taslim) mean submission. And Allah is the one who grants success to what is correct.

When He, glorified be He, forbade harming him (ﷺ) and urged bringing joy to him, He threatened those who harm him. He said, either as a new statement or as a causal explanation, indicating that neglecting any of the prayers and greetings upon him is a form of harm. He emphasized this to make it apparent, because it is something that deserves emphasis, and so that everyone who speaks of it has the utmost eagerness to establish it: ﴿Indeed, those who harm﴾, meaning, those who act as harmers by committing what indicates neglect, out of everything that contradicts ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One than whom there is none greater and whose favor is the only source of any blessing they have, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, meaning the one who has a claim upon them, because of what he tells them about Allah, by which he rescues them from the wretchedness of both abodes and secures for them the happiness of both, a claim they cannot fully repay through gratitude, through any kind of harm, even in falling short in sending prayers upon him with their tongues. ﴿He has cursed them﴾, meaning He has distanced them, expelled them, and made them hateful, ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One than whom there is no greater, ﴿in this world﴾ by driving them to what brings about wrath (p-410), ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ by admitting them to the abode of humiliation.

Since the motive for harming is contempt, He said: ﴿And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾

When the greatest of the harms done to him (ﷺ) was harm done to those who followed him, and since the followers, not being infallible, could conceivably be harmed for the truth, He said, restricting the statement by what it conveys: ﴿And those who harm the believing men﴾, i.e., those firmly established in the attribute of faith, ﴿and the believing women﴾ likewise. And since harm by lying is more severe in corruption and greater in injury, He said: ﴿without their having earned it﴾, i.e., without anything they had committed, deliberately and intentionally, that would make harming them permissible. ﴿Then they have borne a slander﴾, i.e., they have burdened themselves by taking upon themselves ﴿a slander﴾, i.e., a lie and a wickedness exceeding the limit, entailing disgrace in this world. And since there are people on whom shame has no effect, and since harm may occur by means other than speech, He said: ﴿and a manifest sin﴾, i.e., a sin extremely evident, entailing punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 59:

When Allah, glorified is He, forbade harming the believing women, and free women were far from the greed of the corrupters, because of the protection they possess in themselves and the care that men have for them, while a group of people of suspicion (ahl al-rayba) would follow the slave women when they went out, pursuing them for corruption, and free women would go out at night for their needs, it would happen that one of the people of suspicion followed a woman among them (p-411) thinking her to be a slave woman, or knowing that she was a free woman yet pretending that he had thought her a slave woman, and so he would approach her. Sometimes he would return and say to his companions, "I did such-and-such with her," while he was lying, and there would be among the people one who knows that she is so-and-so, and thereby there would result harm beyond what description can encompass. Nor was there at that time, as is reported from Muqatil, any distinction between the free woman and the slave woman; they would go out in a shift and a khimar, and the marking of free women with a sign by which they are recognized (so that they would be held in awe and be modest) would lessen this evil. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Prophet﴾, addressing him with the attribute that is the source of knowledge and wisdom, because the context concerns a wisdom by which the sanctity of the women is defended, so that his thought, peace be upon him, is not occupied with the harm that befalls them, away from receiving (some of) the divine revelations. ﴿Say to your wives﴾: He began with them because of the bond of marriage they have with him. ﴿And your daughters﴾: He mentioned them second because of the bond they have with him and the nobility they possess in themselves; and he placed them after the wives because his wives suffice him in their affairs. ﴿And the women of the believers, let them draw down﴾, i.e., let them bring near, ﴿upon themselves﴾, i.e., upon their faces and all their bodies, so that they leave none of it uncovered, ﴿from their jalabib﴾, and they should not imitate the slave women in their clothing when they go out for their needs by uncovering the hair and the like, thinking that this is more concealing and more protecting for them. The jilbab is the qamis, and a wide garment below the milhafa that a woman wears; and the milhafa is that which covers the clothing; or the khimar, which is whatever covers the head. Al-Baghawi said: the jilbab is the wrapper with which a woman wraps herself above the dir' and the khimar. Hamza al-Kirmani said: Al-Khalil said: everything with which one covers oneself, whether a cover, a garment, or a cloak, is a jilbab. All of these may be intended here. If the intended meaning is the qamis, then drawing it down means completing it until it covers her hands and feet; if it is what covers the head, then drawing it down means covering her face and neck; if it is what covers the garments, then drawing it down means lengthening and widening it so that it conceals her whole body and garments; and if the intended meaning is what is below the milhafa, then the intended meaning is covering the face and hands.

When He commanded this, He gave the reason for it by His saying: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the covering, ﴿is better﴾, i.e., closer than leaving it, ﴿that they may be known﴾ as free women by what distinguishes them from the slave women, ﴿so that they are not﴾, i.e., so that as a consequence of their being known, they ﴿will not be harmed﴾ by those who pursue the slave women. Thus your heart is not occupied away from receiving what comes to you of the divine tidings. When He, glorified is He, elevated them by this command into the presences of good pleasure, they feared the consequence of what they had been in of error by imitating the slave women, so He, glorified is He, informed them that He is in the station of generosity and kindness, and said: ﴿And Allah is﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs absolute perfection, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿Forgiving﴾, i.e., erasing sins both in their essence and their traces, ﴿Merciful﴾, bestowing honor upon whoever turns to Him, obeys His commands, and avoids His prohibitions. Al-Baghawi said: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: (p-413) A slave girl wearing a veil passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and he struck her with his whip and said: "Woe to you! Do you imitate the free women? Cast off the veil."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 60:

Since those who caused harm in the past, and others besides them, were the people of hypocrisy (nifaq) and those close to them, He warned them by His saying, emphatically, to repel their assumption that He would overlook them: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, that is, from harm, ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, that is, one close to hypocrisy, driven to sins, ﴿and the agitators in Madinah﴾, and they are those who spread alarming news among the people of Islam, news by which hearts are shaken, whether they were of the first two categories or not, ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾, by making you驱 [inclined] to be zealous against them, by commanding you to humiliate them, removing the obstacles to that and establishing the causes that lead to it, until you become attached to all their wealth with the adhesion of a thing that is glued with glue, so that they will not be able to get free from anything of what you do to them except by departing from Madinah, through death or by moving to another place. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, as narrated from him by al-Bukhari: "We will surely empower you over them."

Since their removal from Madinah was very unlikely for them, and since it was a greater degree of harm to them than anything else, because expulsion from one's homeland is among the greatest humiliations, (p-414) He indicated it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then they will not be your neighbours therein﴾, that is, after your attempt with them, ﴿except for a little﴾, that is, a little time, sufficient for you to have a place of residence, so that calamities will be severe upon them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 61:

Since the meaning of the speech is that they are to be expelled, because the Prophet (ﷺ) is commanded to banish them, remove them and kill them, he explained their condition in their expulsion, or (the word) is in the accusative by way of reproach [so he said]: ﴿Cursed﴾, meaning: they shall be expelled with the expulsion of distance from mercy and the driving away from the gates of acceptance.

Since the one who is driven away may be left alone and kept at a distance, he explained that they are in other than that condition, so he said, resuming: ﴿Wherever they are found﴾, meaning: they are found, and the one who finds them is more cunning than them, more perceptive, more astute and more skilful, ﴿they shall be seized﴾, meaning: that finder seizes them, ﴿and killed with a thorough killing﴾, meaning: their killing is multiplied and carried to excess. Then he emphasised it with the verbal noun, expressing hatred for them and terrifying them, so he said: ﴿a killing﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 62:

When He had established for them this terrible punishment in this world, He made clear that this was His way with His friends and His enemies. He said, emphasizing it by placing it in the position of the verbal noun, because of their sense that this was far-fetched, since they had never seen the like of it, together with their attachment to family and clans: ﴿Such has been the way of Allah﴾, meaning: the One encompassing all greatness has followed this practice for you, as is His manner, ﴿with those who passed away before﴾, meaning: whose days and reports have gone by and whose events and lifetimes have ended, from among those who used to be hypocrites toward the prophets, like Qarun and his followers. He indicated their killing by specifying that it occurred at some (p-415) of the times, so He said: ﴿from before﴾. The greatest emphasis, given their sense of far-fetchedness which emboldened them toward hypocrisy, is in His words: ﴿and you will never find in the way of Allah any change﴾, meaning: ever and forever, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: the practice of the Supreme King, ﴿any alteration﴾, as the customs of kings are altered, because He does not alter it, and there is no one near to Him in greatness who could be capable of altering it.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 33, verse 63:

When God, exalted is He, had explained what He has prepared in this world for the enemies of His religion, and explained that His way is a straight path that is never broken, because of the laws of wisdom and the varieties of perfection and greatness it contains, and because among the greatest of the judgments and the knowledge of unseen matters is the Hour, and He had [already presented what stirs the question about it in His words: ﴿May God curse them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ (al-Ahzab: 57), and He had] already passed at the end of the sura that they asked, mockingly and in denial, about the specific time of it, and He, glorified is He, threatened them for this question, He said, exalted is He, again threatening them for that and explaining what awaits the enemies of the religion who mock in the Hereafter: ﴿The people ask you﴾, i.e., the polytheists, mockingly. He expressed it this way to indicate that they, still in their swaying, had not reached even the lowest rank of the people of faith, so those who waver in their opinions are hardly ever free of swaying, which is agitation, ﴿about the Hour﴾, i.e., about determining its time.

(p-416) And since their persistence in asking about it was the act of one who thinks that someone other than Him, glorified is He, knows it, He emphasized and said: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., in answer to them: ﴿The knowledge of it is only with God﴾, i.e., the One whose knowledge encompasses all qualities, and who possesses all the attributes of beauty and majesty. He knows what is with everyone, and no one knows anything of what is with Him except by His permission.

And since one of the benefits of knowing the time of a thing is to guard against it or to repel it, He said, indicating the intensity of its concealment by hiding it from the most perfect of His creation, hoping for its nearness as a threat to them: ﴿And what will make you know?﴾, i.e., what thing will inform you of its time? Then He resumed His words: ﴿Perhaps the Hour﴾, i.e., the one which, in reality, has no other hour, because of its wonders, ﴿will be﴾, i.e., will exist and occur in a terrible and wondrous manner, ﴿soon﴾, i.e., in a near time. It is also possible that the masculine form is used because the question about it is in fact a question about determining its time. Al-Bukhari said in the Sahih (al-Sahih, the collection of al-Bukhari): "When you describe a feminine noun as an attribute, you say qarībah (near); when you make it an adverb or a substitute and do not intend it as an attribute, you drop the feminine ending, and likewise its form is the same for the singular, the dual and the plural, masculine and feminine." The purpose of expressing it with la'alla (perhaps) is that it is such that one who hopes for its nearness hopes for it, and one who fears it fears it. So does the one who fears it prepare something to repel it when it comes, or a means of salvation from it when it approaches?

Then he resumed informing about the state of those who ask about it (the Hour), with the phrase, emphasizing it in response to the disbelievers' denial that there is any deficiency in their state: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ (p-417), i.e., the Greatest King, than whom there is no greater, ﴿has cursed﴾, i.e., removed far away, a great removal, from His mercy, ﴿the disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who conceal what it is within their nature to make manifest of what sound intellects indicate concerning it, whether they are opponents or hypocrites, ﴿and has prepared for them﴾, i.e., brought into being and readied from now for their denial of it and of other things whose proofs He has made clear to them, ﴿a blaze﴾, i.e., a fire of intense kindling and blazing.

Since punishment may sometimes be held lightly by some people when it is cut off, even if it is severe, He said, explaining their state: ﴿Abiding therein﴾. And since a thing may sometimes be applied to what resembles it in some respect, metaphorically and by way of exaggeration, He said, emphasizing that the literal meaning is intended: ﴿forever﴾. And since a thing may be intended and then some obstacle prevents it, He said, explaining their state in this condition: ﴿they will find no protector﴾ [i.e.] one who takes charge of a matter that concerns them, by intercession or otherwise, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would give them victory.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 66:

When He mentioned these two states of theirs, He followed it with another state of theirs, a verbal one, in a manner that clarified a physical state, so He said: ﴿The Day﴾, i.e., the measure of their abiding therein in that condition, the Day ﴿when their faces are turned over﴾, i.e., turned over much and severely, ﴿as roasted meat is turned over, and as you see a piece of meat in the pot, with the boiling moving it from one side to another, from one state to another.﴾ He mentioned this even though that fire is independent of it (i.e., of turning), because its encompassing is complete; for mentioning it is more terrifying because of the imagery it contains. He specified the faces because they are the most noble, and the event (ḥadath) occurring upon them is more painful.

Since the explicit noun (al-iẓhār) carries additional clarification and terror, along with conveying that what is in it is an independent statement by itself, He said: ﴿in the Fire﴾, i.e., the kindled one, while they are ﴿saying﴾, and they are in the place of recompense, and the place that accepts action has passed, wishing for what they cannot remedy, because they find nothing that they could estimate would cool their thirst from a protector, nor a helper, nor anything else, except this wish: ﴿O would that we had obeyed God﴾, i.e., in the world, ﴿God﴾, i.e., the One whom we now know to be the King, with whom no one has any command.

Since the situation calls for intensifying submission and humility, they repeated the governing verb and said: ﴿and obeyed the Messenger﴾, i.e., the one who conveyed to us, so that we might be protected from this punishment. The addition of the alif in the reading of the one who wrote it indicates that they take pleasure in mentioning him and believe that his greatness cannot be confined.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 67:

﴿And they say﴾ when nothing benefited them, being disconnected from supplication against those who misled them with that which cures no sick person and quenches no thirst: ﴿"Our Lord"﴾, meaning, "O You who are good to us." They dropped the particle of address (ya) in accordance with the custom of the people of special closeness to the Presence, in order to increase the tenderness, by showing that they have no intermediary except their humiliation and brokenness, which is known in this world to be the greatest cause of God's turning toward His servant. Likewise, the affirming of the particle of distance in saying "O Allah" indicates the lowness of their station and their distance through the abundance of their sins and heedlessness, out of humility before their Lord, so that perhaps He will lift that distance from them.

And since they used to think that following their great ones was not misguidance, but then it became clear to them that this was otherwise, they emphasized their statement for this reason, and to inform that they had cast off the ignorance that was with them, so they are now upon insight into their affair: ﴿"Indeed, we obeyed our masters﴾ (sadatana), and it was also read in the plural with alif and ta' as a sound plural of the broken plural (sadat / sādāt), ﴿"and our great ones, and they misled us"﴾, meaning, as a result of that, they misled us by the influence of the word they possessed, ﴿"from the way"﴾ (al-sabila), as is the habit of the one in error who shifts blame onto others with what does not benefit him. The reading of those who affirm the alif (al-sabīlā) indicates that it is a very wide, clear path, and that it is something to be savored, and that its grandeur must be magnified.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 68:

Since it was as if it were said: "What do you want for them?", they said, exaggerating in tenderness and supplication by repeating "the Lord": ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who are good to us, ﴿give them double punishment﴾, [that is] twice the measure of our punishment, arising from the weakness of our strength and the severity of what affects us, multiplied into many manifold increases, ﴿of the punishment﴾: a double portion for their own misguidance, and another for their misguiding others. If you review what was said in the closing verses of Surat Subhan about the meaning of doubling (ḍi'f), this will become clear to you. This is supported by His saying: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾, that is, drive them away from the places of mercy with a driving that is extreme in number. The meaning according to the reading of Asim with the letter ba' (kabīran, "great") is: mighty, severe, harsh.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 69:

Since the cause of this whole threat was what they deliberately did of harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by their saying, "He married his son's wife," and other things, up until He concluded it with what would be a cause for their wishing to obey him; and hearing this was a kindness (lutf) to whoever believed in it, He followed it with what is like its result, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, who affirmed what was recited to them, ﴿do not be⟩ by your harming the Messenger (ﷺ), whether regarding the matter of Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her) or otherwise, a state that is like a nature for you ﴿like those who harmed Moses⟩ from among his people, the Children of Israel, who harmed him with various kinds of harm, as our Prophet (ﷺ) said when he distributed a portion and some people spoke about it, so he said: "Moses was harmed with more than this, and he was patient." And the thing most suited to the meaning here is the harm Qarun inflicted upon him by the prostitute whom he hired to accuse him with herself [so Allah cleared him of that, and it was the cause of the sinking of Qarun and those with him], ﴿so Allah cleared him﴾, meaning, as a consequence of their harming him, He cleared him, ﴿Allah⟩, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of majesty and beauty, and power (p-421) over every thing, and perfection. [The expression with the form of intensification (tafʿīl) conveys that the clearing came gradually: by the sinking, by the sudden death, and by the shining of Aaron's staff, as passed at the end of the stories.] When He forbade resembling those who harm, in general, whether their harm was verbal or practical, He indicated that the harm intended here is verbal, like the matter of Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her), so He said: ﴿from what they said⟩ [rather than saying "from what they did," and that is] by what He showed of proof of his truthfulness, so He sank whoever harmed him, as passed in the stories. So beware, then beware.

Since their aim in this harm was to bring down his standing, He said: ﴿And he was⟩, meaning Moses, peace be upon him, in a firm state, ﴿with Allah⟩, meaning the One who does not humiliate whoever He befriends, ﴿honored (wajīhan)⟩, meaning esteemed, of high rank, whenever he asks Him, He gives him. And if he was with Allah in this station, he was with the people in it too, because of what they saw of Allah's honoring him. [The sentence serves as a reason for the clearing, since one is not cleared except by someone who is honored in His sight.]

When He forbade them from causing harm, He commanded them to do good, so that they might become honored before Him, Glorified is He. He repeated the call (to them) to solicit their attention and to show concern, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: "you who claim that." Since He had, at the beginning of the surah, specifically addressed the Prophet ﷺ with the command to have taqwa, He at its end generalized the command to have taqwa, following up their prohibition with a command that implies a warning, so that the deterrent from harm and the motivation to abandon it would be strengthened. So He said: ﴿Fear Allah﴾, meaning: "Be truthful in your claim by fearing the One who possesses all greatness. Make for yourselves a shield (wiqayah) against His wrath (sukht) by surrendering to Him all of the trust (amanah) He has deposited with you." ﴿And speak﴾ concerning the Prophet ﷺ in the matter of Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, and others, and concerning his daughters and wives, may Allah be pleased with them, and concerning the believers and their wives, and other than that, ﴿a words of upright correctness﴾, meaning: aiming at the truth, correct and right in what it says.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 71:

﴿He will set right for you your deeds﴾, meaning: by causing you to enter upon righteous action, while you do not know the proper manner of it; so He makes you perceive it little by little, and enables you to act upon what He has made clear to you, until you are upon the most complete, greatest, most pleasing and most upright way, through the blessing of your speaking the truth in the good and beautiful manner.

Since man, however diligent he is, is deficient, He said, indicating this so that he will never cease to acknowledge his incapacity: ﴿and He will forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: He will erase them both in essence and in trace, so that He does not punish for them nor reproach for them. And since it might be supposed that this applies only to those who believe, and that renewing faith is not beneficial, He removed this supposition by His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾, meaning the One than whom there is nothing greater, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, meaning the one whose greatness is from His greatness, by renewing obedience to them through faith and its fruits at every time, so that he is one who renders the trust to its people, ﴿then he has certainly attained a great attainment﴾. He emphasized this by His saying: ﴿a great attainment﴾, meaning succeeding in achieving all of his aims in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 72:

Since the implied meaning is: "And whoever does not obey has indeed suffered a manifest loss," and since everything that is presented to something makes that to which it is presented capable of it and empowered over it, [and] since every thing that God has entrusted to something, which guards and preserves it and gives it to its people and delivers it, is one who gives up the trust without bearing it, and everyone who entrusts something to another and it is lost, and who takes responsibility for it on behalf of its people and withholds it from its rightful recipient, is a traitor concerning it who bears it; and since God the Exalted has entrusted to people the intellects by which they distinguish between the sound and the corrupt, and the apparent faculties by which they direct them toward whatever they wish of disobedience and obedience, then among them is one who uses his intellect to infer the truth and falsehood alike, and so he gives up from his faculties what he deserves, and thus he is one who gives up the trust without bearing it. Among them is one who does the opposite, and they are the majority, so he is one who bears it [it] and is a traitor concerning it in what he was commanded to give up. And God, glorified is He, entrusted the cosmos with what benefits it, from waters, minerals and plants, and it gave that up and did not withhold it from anyone who sought it, although its withholding it was within the realm of possibility. God the Exalted said, giving a reason for the command to piety, or beginning a new statement emphasizing it, as an alert that this matter deserves to be emphasized as an alert to its subtlety, and that it is something that few people almost ever perceive, let alone affirm it [turning the speech to the manifestation of greatness as an indication of the great audacity of man]: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾, that is, its discharge, or its bearing, or withholding it from its people, and it is His obedience, glorified is He, in what He commanded the rational being and in what He willed from others. He did not mention the waters and the winds, because they are among what is in the two worlds of trusts which they discharge according to the command. ﴿to the heavens﴾ with what is in them of benefits, ﴿and the earth﴾ with what is in it of conveniences and minerals. When the generalization was intended to be made explicit, He said: ﴿and the mountains﴾ [and] because most benefits are in them, ﴿and they refused﴾ despite the greatness of their bodies, the strength of their foundations and the vastness of their expanses, ﴿to bear it﴾, so they would withhold it and keep it from its people. Al-Zamakhshari said: from your saying, "So-and-so bears the trust and carries it," that is, he does not deliver it to its owner until it leaves his charge and is removed from his responsibility, because the trust is as if it were riding the one entrusted with it, and he is its bearer. Do you not see that they say: "debts have ridden him, and I have a right over him"? So when he discharges it, it no longer rides him, nor is he its bearer. ﴿And they feared it﴾, so each of them gave up what God had entrusted to it at its time as God willed it, and this is the meaning of ﴿We came willingly﴾. The summary is that the will, which is the creational command regarding the cosmos, was made to apply because they do not understand, like the obligatory creational command in regard to us, because we understand, distinguishing between one who understands and one who does not in judgment, just as He distinguished between them in understanding, giving each of them what it deserves in its rank. This is the meaning of what al-Baghawi transmitted from al-Zajjaj and others of the scholars of meanings. How excellent is what al-Nabigha Ziyad ibn Mu'awiya al-Dhubyani said, when he said:

"I came to you stripped, my garments worn thin, in fear, and suspicion is cast upon me.
So I found the trust, it did not betray it, and thus was Nuh, who did not betray."

Ibn al-Furat said: when it was said to Umar, may God be pleased with him, that al-Nabigha was the one who said both of them, he said: "He is the best of your poets."

And since the traitor is many times more numerous than the trustworthy, and since the self, with what is placed in it of desires and appetites, is the locus of deficiencies, God the Exalted said: ﴿but man bore it﴾, that is, most people and jinn, for "al-insan" is mankind, and "al-ins" and "al-unas" are people. It was previously mentioned in ﴿and do not diminish people's things﴾ [al-A'raf: 85] in al-A'raf that "al-nas" may comprise humans and jinn, and that it is the plural of "ins," whose root is "unas." Attribution to the category does not necessarily mean that every individual within it is so; here it is according to the majority. In the expression with it there is an indication that only one who is at the lowest ranks, who has not reached the limit of stupor, betrays.

And since man, because of what he has of intimacy with himself, and in his attributes of passion, and in what he has of intellect and understanding, thinks that there is no deficiency in him, He gave the reason for that by saying, emphasizing: ﴿Indeed he﴾, despite the weakness of his strength and the scarcity of his resources, ﴿was﴾ (that is, in his nature, except those whom God protects) ﴿a wrongdoer﴾, who places a thing in other than its place, like one who is in darkness because his desires have covered his intellect, and for this reason He said: ﴿ignorant﴾, that is, his ignorance overcomes his forbearance so it leads him into wrongdoing. Thus each of the manifestation of what God entrusted in the cosmos and its being within the realm of possibility is made as if it were presented to them, every one who bears it and gives it up, just as He made the empowerment of man over each of revealing what he was entrusted with and concealing it likewise.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 33, verse 73:

When the judgment (al-hukm) was, outwardly, upon all of mankind, but in reality, since a proposition lacking quantifiers (al-qadiyya al-khaliya 'an al-suwar) is in effect particular (juz'iyya), upon part of them; yet when it was stated in the absolute manner of a universal, it was understood that the intended meaning is the majority. He said, clarifying that "al" (in al-insan) is not a quantifier, giving as the reason for his bearing it (the trust) that he [man] had been subjected to punishment, indicating that the treacherous (al-khawana) are the majority, [turning the expression to the Greatest Name to diversify the discourse between majesty and beauty]: ﴿That Allah may punish﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, because of treachery in the trust. He placed first [from among the treacherous] those most deserving of it, saying: ﴿the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾, i.e., those who display the surrender of the trust falsely and deceitfully, while they carry it and are deeply rooted in hypocrisy; ﴿and the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾, i.e., those who openly declare their bearing of it and their withholding it from its people, [and they are deeply rooted in polytheism, so they do not repent of it].

Since placing the punishment first implies that the treacherous are the majority, he indicated that (p-427) the sincere is exceedingly rare by his saying: ﴿and Allah will turn in forgiveness﴾, i.e., by what He has of greatness, ﴿toward the believing men﴾, i.e., those who are deeply rooted in the attribute of faith, namely those who remain steadfast upon it until death, ﴿and the believing women﴾, the disobedient and others, so He grants them success in surrendering it after bearing it. [The verse is of the method of ihtibak: He mentioned the punishment first as an indication of the blessing second, and the repentance second as an indication of the withholding first.] That is, He presented this presentation and passed this judgment [the judgment] in order to punish and to bestow favour, with a wisdom that people recognise among themselves.

Since this indicates that there is no one who has not borne it at some time, it was both encouraging to hearts and cautioning to souls. He said, comforting them and encouraging them: ﴿And Allah has always been﴾, i.e., upon what He has of majesty, greatness, retribution, dominion and might, ﴿Forgiving﴾, i.e., erasing the sins of those who repent, both actual and potential, in essence and in effect, ﴿Merciful﴾, i.e., honouring them with all kinds of honour after returning from transgression. When He commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) at its opening to fear God, He commanded him at its close with that in a general manner, and He threatened the dissenters and hypocrites whom He forbade in its beginning from obeying them, and He concluded with the two attributes of forgiveness and mercy as He concluded at its beginning with them the verse of error and intention. Thus they met, embraced, agreed and corresponded. And Allah speaks the truth, and [He] guides to the way, and He knows best what is right.
